articles.headline: Exclusive details about Akai’s MPC Sample Key
keyFacts: Akai teased the new MPC Sample Key and stated it plans to open-source the software.
Exclusive images show the instrument is designed for pitched sample playback rather than chopping drums.
A launch date and price have not been announced yet.
body: Akai teased its new MPC Sample Key on Instagram earlier this week, and said it plans to open-source its software so the modding community can hack it to their hearts’ delight. While there’s no word yet on when the device will launch or how much it will cost, The Verge has received exclusive images of the upcoming instrument that offer some details about its feature set.
Exclusive details about Akai’s MPC Sample Key
The open-source MPC Sample Key won’t be focused on chopping up drum breaks.

While the Sample Key shares many of the same controls as the MPC Sample — including the three context-sensitive encoders, a large main encoder — it seems designed for pitched sample playback, rather than chopping up drums. In fact, the “chop” button from the MPC Sample is missing entirely from the Sample Key.

The dedicated pitch and mod wheels are another clue there. But there are also buttons for changing the octave range of the 37-key keyboard, as well as ones labeled “chord” and “arp.” Presumably, those enable a chord playback mode and an arpeggiator. While using an arpeggiator to play back drum samples can be a fun way to create rhythms, it’s more commonly used for melodic and bass parts. And a chord mode would be basically useless for drums. Those options also appear to replace the chop function from the standard MPC Sample.

There also appears to be a dedicated looper that could be useful for live performance and layering sounds. And, instead of the Flex Beat effects from the original MPC Sample, there’s something called “Swarm.” Though what that is isn’t exactly clear at the moment.

Like the first entry in the Sample series, the Key has a built-in mic and speaker for all-in-one music production. While we haven’t gotten a glimpse at the back panel yet, the config options on the front suggest that, in addition to MIDI, the Sample Key will have CV outs for integrating with modular synths.

articles.headline: The Worst GTA Game Is One Rockstar Could Never Make Today
keyFacts: Polygon reported that GTA Advance is a flawed Game Boy Advance prequel that serves as an essential part of Rockstar history.
The article stated that developer Digital Eclipse and Rockstar struggled with the hardware limitations of the Game Boy Advance.
The publication noted that the game provided a necessary learning experience for Rockstar to develop better portable titles later.
body: GTA Advance is an odd game. It's terrible in some ways, yet also not as bad as its reputation suggests. It's also an essential part of Rockstar history. This was Rockstar at a stage of uncertainty. The essence of the Grand Theft Auto franchise was still in flux, and the studio had yet to firmly decide on what, exactly, made a GTA game. GTA Advance has its strong points, but the most important thing about it is how it gave Rockstar (via developer Digital Eclipse) a chance to see where the series could fall short. It's a necessary bad game that paved the way for better ones — and the kind of essential failure the games industry can't tolerate anymore.

GTA Advance is a sort of loose GTA 3 prequel, with "loose" being the operative word. It takes place in Liberty City before GTA 3's Claude gets shot by his girlfriend, though you'd be hard-pressed to recognize Liberty City landmarks here (more on that in a bit). The star of GTA Advance is Mike, a petty criminal who — rather like Niko in GTA 4 — really doesn't want a life of crime anymore. But this is GTA, and a life of crime is what Mike gets. The mafia kills his friend and partner-in-crime Vinnie, just as the two were about to leave Liberty City behind for good, and Mike gets embroiled in a revenge scheme to get back at the organized crime group. Not a smart idea on his part, but an exciting one nonetheless.

Mike's missions involve tracking down information about Vinnie's murderer, a dangerous game that gets him closer to the mafia with every new lead. It's loaded with scrunchy pixel melodrama, and there's a highly satisfying twist at the end that turns the whole story on its head. Rockstar is no stranger to vengeance tales or high-stakes crime drama, but modern GTA often has very loose stories. C.J. wants revenge in San Andreas, Tommy's grudge is what keeps him in Vice City, and so on. But often, you feel disconnected from that need for revenge. The event that sparks it is so far removed from you and the character, or so clichéd, that it's not a compelling motivation. The need to explore every corner of the city is what pushes you forward more. Mike's story, despite occasionally veering into GTA 3 fan fiction territory, has a more immediate sense of urgency to it. That better life was so close and then someone yanked it right out from under you for no good reason.

Mike's struggles take a backseat to your struggle of getting through GTA Advance, though. Digital Eclipse and Rockstar's ambition outstripped the Game Boy Advance's capabilities, and the poor little system struggles to keep up with the game. Framerates are awful, and the controls are terribly clunky. Well, most Rockstar games have clunky controls, but when everything you need to do is confined to fewer buttons laid out across a smaller space, things get more complicated than they need to be.

Which is a shame, as GTA Advance is a fascinating look at GTA's adolescence, one worth examining even if it does suck to play. It's Rockstar in an uncharacteristically indecisive moment, trying to fuse modern GTA with the series' classic top-down style, marketed to an audience that probably didn't plan on buying a GTA game when they picked up the tiny purple handheld. GTA Advance tries adapting the open-ended nature of its 3D siblings to the hardware constraints of the Game Boy Advance, and Rockstar even marketed it as a continuation of the 3D games.

"The legendary, rule-breaking and genre-defying Grand Theft Auto franchise has arrived on the Game Boy Advance," the game's promotional material read. "Return to the streets of Liberty City in a brand-new story, all new missions, and classic open-ended Grand Theft Auto gameplay."

That was wishful thinking on Rockstar's part. The open-endedness is reserved for exploring the city — rendered fantastically, it must be said, even if it wasn't as visually astounding as its contemporaries — and to a lesser extent, taking on side missions. Mike's critical story path is linear, though the side missions aren't too different from what you'd find in Vice City. You've got your street races, firefighting missions, vigilante missions, all the stuff Rockstar loaded in modern GTA. Just in a much smaller, choppier package with worse radio stations. Those details may seem trivial, but Rockstar soon learned they were hugely important to its audience.

But that's okay! Playing GTA Advance is much less fun than talking about GTA Advance, but bad games are necessary. No one produces perfection the first time out. The modern games industry has no room for underperforming or less-than-perfect games anymore. Hell, it barely has room for best-sellers anymore. Room for iteration and improvement is essential, though, and you can look at Rockstar's later portable GTA games as an example. Chinatown Wars for the Nintendo DS and PlayStation Portable (developed in-house by Rockstar) met with warm praise, which singled out just how expertly Rockstar adapted the soul of GTA to a more restrictive format. GTA Advance might be a crummy game, but that crumminess and determining what doesn't work for GTA, was an essential stepping stone for the series' future.

articles.headline: AI companies flew too close to the sun: tech sector stock selloff sees Intel take the biggest hit
keyFacts: A massive tech sector stock selloff occurred after several companies reported subpar earnings and negative revenue impacts from AI.
Hardware producer Intel took the biggest hit, dropping over 30 percent and nearing its 1971 IPO levels.
Other companies including Google, Nvidia, AMD, Micron, and SK Hynix also experienced stock value reductions during the selloff.
body: AI has infested the world as no parasite had ever done before. Forget The Last of Us and its cordyceps: this thing somehow finds its way even into places that never had a thing to do with AI before. Printers, the agricultural sector, even your plumbing and communal upkeep services are turning into AI companies now and taking multibillion IPOs. Why? It’s a fad, a trend. And maybe it’s on its way out.

After several tech companies reported on subpar earnings, and some even on how AI seems to have ruined their revenue streams, a massive stock selloff was triggered, taking hardware producer Intel down by over 30 percent and putting it on track to go below its 1971 IPO levels. The Nasdaq-100 is down 10 percent since Oct. 6, and just about every single company related to AI took a hit, big or small.

Photo by Igor Omilaev Google (Alphabet) dropped 12.49 percent in the last five days following an earnings report that allegedly indicated AI overviews butchered its main revenue stream. It is now sitting lower than in October 2025 and is down 27 percent compared to six months ago.

Nvidia’s stock price went down almost 20 bucks, or about 10 percent, in five days, but it has since regained a bit of its lost value. AMD, its main competitor, lost 10 percent of its stock value during today alone.

Micron, one of the main producers of DRAM in the industry and an absolutely vital part of the current AI boom, also saw a reduction, with 5.5 percent of its stock wiped out on Oct. 30. SK Hynix, its brother-in-arms in RAM production, went down around eight percent. Across the board, shareholders are panicking and selling off their stock, driving stock prices down.
China’s stock market is also seeing a huge dip, also primarily involving AI-focused corporations.

Whether this is a blatant short or market manipulation meant to devalue these supergiants so big investors could buy the dip and make untold amounts of money is unknown, but I would not be surprised. The AI market is propped up by fictional cash, incredible losses, and trillions of dollars going around in circles, passed around between Nvidia, AMD, RAM producers, data center builders, and cloud computing companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and others.
Eventually, though, the snake will eat its own tail, and that, my friends, will be a sight to behold.

articles.headline: Fans Think Blizzard Is Teasing A Return To Its Most Beloved Setting In World Of Warcraft: Forever
keyFacts: World of Warcraft fans spotted potential easter eggs in a launch trailer pointing to a return to the continent Northrend.
Principal game designer Kris Zierhut stated that Northrend exists in the game, though the launch focuses on Kalimdor and Eastern Kingdoms.
Lead Classic designer Tim Jones suggested players could potentially visit a hostile level-60 version of Northrend in the future.
body: As World of Warcraft: Forever‘s release next week approaches, fans have combed through a brand new launch trailer and found what they think is an easter egg signifying something massive: a potential return to the beloved continent of Northrend that was featured in WoW‘s Wrath of the Lich King expansion.
The easter egg is in this trailer, which came out earlier this week to celebrate the launch with a sick animation set to…oh my god is that Amy Lee in “End of You”? Oh, hell yes.

You want to watch at around the 3:00 minute mark, where it shows a zoomed-out version of Azeroth with lots of blue and red lights coming from continents to the left- and right-hand sides. Those continents are, of course, Kalimdor and Eastern Kingdoms, the two continents we’ll be exploring when Forever launches. In the middle is a big, cloudy mass: that’s the Maelstrom. No one’s in there, it’s a dang Maelstrom.
But what’s that to the north?

As pointed out by Whatdididotho1 on Reddit, there are, faintly visible, some glowing red and blue lights on top of the map on a landmass to the north. That’s Northrend, the icy northern continent originally depicted in Warcraft 3 and, later, given an entire WoW expansion to shine in Wrath of the Lich King, which is largely regarded as one of the game’s best expansions even years later. Why would there be little lights up there if not to indicate that players might be up there? There’s no way this is some sort of silly oversight.

Blizzard itself isn’t denying the possibility, and in fact seems to encourage the speculation. In a recent interview with IGN, principal game designer Kris Zierhut confirmed that “Northrend exists” in Forever, as do Pandaria and the Dark Portal, as all these locations had been canonized at the time that World of Warcraft first came out. However, Zierhut also says that this game is intended to focus on Kalimdor and Eastern Kingdoms. There will be no new capital cities: you’ll always return “home,” with Forever being about drilling into those continents in greater detail rather than spreading out into more and more areas.
Still, that doesn’t mean we can’t occasionally visit. Perhaps for a dungeon? Or, as lead Classic designer Tim Jones suggests, a “hostile” max-level zone:

I think our attitude is [that] we are in a kind of a time bubble, right? We’re locked in the place in between the end of Warcraft 3 and before Burning Crusade. And everything about Azeroth existed, even Outland exists, even Northrend exists, like QuelâThelas exists. All these places are there. And I don’t think if we ever went to Northrend, we wouldn’t be visiting the version that you see in Wrath of the Lich King, but could we visit some extremely hostile level 60 version of it because Arthas is still in the stage where he’s sending KelâThuzad to Eastern Kingdoms to assault Eastern Plaguelands? We could. There’s so much that we can do with the timeline that we’re in.

Whatever’s going on in Northrend, we’re not going to see it at launch, but given all these hints I feel like it’s coming imminently, and we’ll start to see breadcrumb hints as we play through the endgame content that hasn’t been seen yet. Personally, I’m glad WoW: Forever isn’t going to keep hopping continents every few years until it abandons its old world altogether. But good as it is to be able to return home, it’s still fun to occasionally poke our nose outside and see what’s going on further afield. Even if it’s a bit chilly out there.

articles.headline: The essential off-grid coffee makers every prepper needs for real espresso in a blackout
keyFacts: TechRadar highlighted off-grid coffee makers, such as the hand-powered Wacaco Nanopresso and the battery-powered Dreame Ecceluxe Go, for emergency blackout supplies.
The article noted that whole coffee beans stored in airtight containers with a manual burr grinder provide better flavor during a crisis.
The Dreame Ecceluxe Go will launch soon in Spain, Portugal, and the United States, while lacking a current UK release plan.
body: So you've got your water, cash, canned food, and a wind-up radio, but something is missing from your prepping supplies. If the power goes out and your water supply is cut, how will you make your morning coffee? Put down that jar of instant granules — basic services might have failed, but your tastebuds haven't.

Drip coffee is an easy way to perk yourself up and boost your morale in a crisis (just pick up a ChemEx brewer or a simple dripper with some filter papers), but if you're aiming to conserve water then a shot of espresso is a better way to get your caffeine fix, so here I've focused on brewers for preparing shorter drinks.

Consider how you're going to store your emergency coffee supply, too. Whole beans will hold their flavor better than ground, and I recommend keeping them in an opaque, airtight container in a cool place (light, heat, air, and moisture are the enemies of aroma compounds). You'll need a grinder, too — look for one with burrs rather than blades so your coffee isn't chopped up in rough pieces.
If all that sounds like too much hassle in a crisis, opt for foil-sealed coffee pods instead. Both the Nanopresso and Dreame Ecceluxe Go below have adapters for brewing with single-serve capsules.

The Ecceluxe Go heats its own water, but if you pick a more basic brewer then you'll need a different way to get it up to temperature. As the former editor of an outdoor gear website, I recommend a simple gas camping stove like the MSR Pocket Rocket 2, which will get your water up to around 203F / 95C in approximately 3.5 minutes. Now, onto the brewers...
Wacaco NanoPresso

No power? No problem. The Wacaco Nanopresso generates up to 18 bars of pressure using nothing but elbow grease. It's small enough to tuck inside a pocket, and is hand-powered, so all you need is a source of hot water to create properly extracted espresso with thick crema (even if you have to use a flashlight to see what you're doing).

The standard Nanopresso uses ground coffee, which you can tamp down using the scoop (the brewer has a valve to release pressure if you accidentally tamp it too hard), but if you'd rather use pods then the NS adaptor allows you to use Nespresso Original style capsules instead.

It feels robust and solid in the hand, and is packed with thoughtful little features like an insulated water tank and cup to protect your hands from heat, and an easy-clean portafilter that needs minimal maintenance.
Dreame Ecceluxe Go

The Dreame Ecceluxe Go is a battery-powered brewer with a miniature boiler built-in. Just pour room-temperature water into the reservoir on top (measuring lines engraved inside will prevent you overfilling it and wasting precious resources), then pick the right adapter — Nespresso Original, Nestlé Dolce Gusto, ESE (Easy Serve Espresso), or fresh grounds — and you're ready to brew.

Preparing an espresso with room temperature water takes about six minutes from start to finish, and you can prepare two or three drinks before the Ecceluxe Go needs recharging (from a portable battery or solar generator during a power outage). The brew unit itself is smaller than a thermos flask, and comes in a compact carry case that you can tuck away with the rest of your emergency supplies.

The Dreame Ecceluxe Go is due to go on sale in Spain and Portugal very soon, with the US following shortly after. There's no plan for a UK launch yet, but it charges via USB-C, so there's no reason British preppers can't import one.
AeroPress and Manual Coffee Grinder

If you're planning to keep whole coffee beans in your emergency supplies, you need the AeroPress Manual Coffee Grinder. I've tested a lot of manual grinders in my time, and this is easily the best. It has proper burrs rather than cheap blades so coffee is ground rather than shredded, and they're adjustable so you can optimize the grind size to suit your brewing method.

The default setting is optimized for the AeroPress brewer, which you can use to make a short, strong shot of coffee to keep you awake, or a longer, smoother drink if you have water to spare. I have a plastic AeroPress in my locker at work (you never know what might happen), but if you want something extra tough then take a look at the rugged AeroPress Steel. If you're part of a whole family of coffee-lovers there's also the king-sized AeroPress XL, and if you need something you can also use on the road, the bijou AeroPress Go packs down into a compact travel cup.

articles.headline: Breeders’ Cup 2026: Folsom Blues set to go off as favourite in Juvenile Turf, day one – live
keyFacts: Billy Loughnane rode Libertango to victory in the opening race of the 2026 Breeders’ Cup at Keeneland after making a late weight change.
Unbeaten filly Sun Goddess is highlighted as a strong European favourite for the Juvenile Fillies’ Turf after winning six of eight starts.
Bob Baffert’s unbeaten runner Hughes is positioned as a strong favourite for the Juvenile dirt event in the absence of USS Valor.
body: The big four came clear in the stretch, but Hughes led coming out of the home turn and his gallop never faltered on the run to the line. He’ll be a serious candidate for the Kentucky Derby next May.
He set off as the 4-5 favourite on the US tote, the same price as Sun Goddess.
A quote has just dropped from earlier, from Billy Loughnane after his first Breeders’ Cup victory (no doubt of many) aboard George Boughey’s Libertango.

“I can’t put it into words. I never expected to ride the filly at this weight. Thankfully, they have the saunas here so I managed to do the weight. I’ve been working on the weight all week … and a big thank you to George Boughey for putting me back on board.”
Sun Goddess was the first odds-on shot of the meeting and Hughes is likely to be the second. He’s currently 3-5 with the local tote, and a similar price with the British books.
20.55 Breeders Cup Juvenile, Grade One, 1m ½f, dirt
Six runners – for the second year running – is a disappointing turnout for the Juvenile, but it has a worthy favourite in the Bob Baffert’s Hughes, who is unbeaten in four starts.
He won the Grade One American Pharoah at Santa Anita by six lengths, going clear easily under a hand ride.

Todd Pletcher’s American History is also unbeaten – in two – and won the Grade One Futurity over track and trip last time. He was not favourite by any stretch, but picked off the first and second favourites late after they had duelled down the stretch. Another of today’s runners, Coach Pope, was the favourite there and perhaps a little unlucky to get picked off after getting the better of his market rival.

Salahudin is also worth a mention as he attempts to give Baffert a record-extending seventh win in this race. He did not have an ideal trip in the Iroquois Stakes at Churchill Downs last time and did well to win in the circumstances.

It’s been a meeting for the favourites so far and it’s hard to see much beyond Hughes here. There’s no obvious pace in the race after Gaudreau was scratched and Flavien Pratt should be able to settle just off the lead and pick his moment.

A masterclass in no-nonsense race-riding from Ryan Moore, who got Sun Goddess out and across from stall nine to sit second as they went into the first turn. She travelled sweetly from there and it was just a case of when Moore pressed the button.
What a remarkable filly she is: eight runs, seven wins, three Group Ones. And on top of all that, she has the physique and scope to be an even better three-year-old.
She set off as the 4-5 favourite on course, what a gift that looks now.

In terms of the likely pace (see pace map below) here, the picture changed somewhat earlier today when Luminous Beauty replaced a non-runner, and she may well be trying to get over from the outside stall along with Seneca Park.

Ryan Moore may well need to drop in on Sun Goddess, while Amusingly will also be coming from off the pace. Green Empress should have a decent pitch against the rail, but in terms of the likely winner, I think this is all about Sun Goddess and probably a question of how far?

Johnny Murtagh has a runner in this race too in Curracloe, unbeaten in two starts, and bidding to become only the third person – after Freddy Head and Joseph O’Brien – to both ride and train a Breeders’ Cup winner.

Libertango’s win in the opener was a big boost for the Cheveley Park form and Sun Princess could well be the first odds-on shot of this year’s Breeders’ Cup. She’s 4-5 on the opening show from the track, with Amusingly next in on 5-1. Domestic Agenda is 6-1 with the patriotic locals, but around 12-1 with the British books according to Oddschecker.
20.15 Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies’ Turf, Grade One, 1m
We’re back on the turf for the next race European-trained runners – and two of those in particular – are likely to dominate the market.

Sun Goddess is already the hot favourite for next year’s 1,000 Guineas and arrives having won six of eight starts so far this year. She started her season as long ago as 9 May but could not have been any more impressive in the Cheveley Park last time.

Amusingly, her main market rival, is two-from-three and won the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere against the colts last time, beating Folsom Blues, the likely favourite for the Juvenile Turf later on the card.
Both fillies are drawn wide, though, while Joseph O’Brien’s Green Empress, the Prix Marcel Boussac winner last time, has a better pitch in one.
The best of the Americans, meanwhile, could well be Chad Brown’s Domestic Agenda, the winner of the Miss Grillo at Belmont, often one of the best trials for this race.

Miss Monica did well to get as close as she did after edging left and bumping at least one rival shortly after the start. That said, Emphatic showed an exceptional turn of foot to storm clear on the turn for home.
Two minutes to post time for the Juvenile Fillies, and Emphatic is the one for money on-course. She’s down to 3-1 on the tote, with Miss Monica steady at 2-1.
Miss Monica has opened as the 2-1 favourite on the US tote, with Emphatic next at 7-2 and Domain Expansion on 9-2.
The unbeaten Manuka Honey deserves a mention too, she is unbeaten in three and showed plenty of determination to get to the lead in the stretch in the Grade Three Pocahontas at Churchill last time.
19.35 Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies, Grade One, dirt, 1m ½f
News on that objection when it arrives, but for now we need to look ahead to the next race on the card, the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies.
The market for the first of the two dirt events is headed by two unbeaten fillies, Emphatic and Miss Monica, while Domain Expansion was an impressive winner switching from turf to dirt last time out.

Emphatic is three-from-three for trainer Brendan Walsh, and her prep includes a win in the Grade One Alcibiades Stakes over track and trip last time out, when she made all the running from the inside stall.
Miss Monica is unbeaten in two for Bob Baffert, both at Del Mar and including the Grade One Debutante Stakes last time, which she won by six-and-a-quarter lengths.
Domain Expansion was an outsider for the Grade Two Oak Leaf Stakes at Santa Anita but went clear to register an easy seven-length success.
It promises to be a tight contest between the three market leaders, but there was a lot to like about Miss Monica’s latest win and she appeals as the likeliest winner.

Fairytale stuff from Billy Loughnane. He broke in mid-division and was forced to wait behind horses before starting to thread his way through, and still had five lengths to make on the leader turning in.
He launched Libertango down the middle of the track and as Ruiva dropped away, he started to make ground relentlessly and then reeled in Hell Of A Spin with a stride to spare.

I can’t be entirely certain about this as I don’t have a Kentucky rulebook to hand, but a commentator on the track feed suggests that if Libertango wins, Flavien Prat will still be due his cut of the prize money because the switch was so late.
George Boughey is chatting to a track reporter about Billy Loughnane’s unexpected appearance on Libertango.

articles.headline: Giants’ 7-round 2027 NFL Draft according to PFF mock draft simulator during bye week

The New York Giants have picked in the top 10 of the NFL Draft in nine of the last 12 years. With a 4-2-1 record in 2026 thus far , they are now sitting at the No. 26 spot in the 2027 NFL Draft. As the team takes its bye week , we asked the PFF 2027 NFL Mock Draft simulator what the G Men might do in April, and this is what it came back with.
Round 1, Pick 26: RB Kewan Lacey, Ole Miss

The Giants have three solid running backs in Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy , and Devin Singletary. However, they are all best as change-of-pace backs, not bell-cow ball-carriers. Whether it is Jaxson Dart or JJ McCarthy under center next season , an RB1 behind them will help a great deal.

Ole Miss’ Kewan Lacey has decent size at 5-foot-11, 205 pounds and has an explosive, home run hitter element to his game that the other three backs currently in the New York backfield do not. His dynamic running ability would give the Big Blue offense a dimension it does not currently have.

The knocks on Lacey are his power and his pass-catching. The good news here is that the Giants already have other packs for that. If they keep Skattebo and Tracey, the team would have those two areas covered (as well as pass protection), and Lacey can just do what he does best, which is rip off big chunks or yards for his squad.
Round 2, Pick 58: CB Evan Johnson, BYU

As you will see in this PFF 2027 NFL Mock Draft simulator run, the Giants need to address their secondary in April. At corner, Deonte Banks is playing well, but the team could use an upgrade over Dru Phillips and Greg Newsome. That’s where BYU’s Evan Johnson comes in.

The Cougars’ corner has enough size at 6 feet, 180 pounds to play on the outside. And he’s being thrown at a lot this season with solid results. He has stood up in both man and zone, with QBs posting just a 43.2 passer rating against him . At worst, he will be a nice rotational corner for the Giants next season, and at best a starter.
Round 3, Pick 90: DT CJ Fite, Arizona State

The Sun Devils’ CJ Fite has good size at 6-foot-2, 310 pounds and is in the upper echelon of run-stuffing defensive tackles in this class. With 4.5 tackles for a loss, he is adept at mucking up the middle of the line and getting into the backfield to drag down running backs. He also has 2.0 sacks on the season, showing there may be some pass-rush upside there, too.
Round 6, Pick 204: S Terry Moore, Ohio State
Round 6, Pick 206: S Rod Moore Jr., Michigan

Javn Holland is having an excellent season for the Giants, ranking fourth overall among all safeties, according to PFF grades. Jason Pinnock isn’t far behind at 19th, but Tyler Nubin is struggling, coming in at 84. So, it would make sense for the Giants to grab some more safeties to help with depth and possibly even starting talent, which is exactly what the PFF 2027 NFL Mock Draft simulator did with the team’s two sixth-round selections.

Terry Moore had a 71-tackle, 7.0-TFL, four-interception season in 2024 at Duke before a knee injury kept him out all of 2025 before transferring to Ohio State. Rod Moore Jr. is a three-year captain at Michigan and a talented safety who picked off six balls in 2022 and 20223. A knee injury cost him the entire 2024 campaign and most of 2025.
Both players are now back and playing well overall, though not at their previous levels. If one or both of them can return to their pre-injury form, they could be a steal in Round 6.

body: Islam Makhachev has declared his next UFC fight will be ‘one of the last of my career.’
Makhachev is set to put his welterweight title on the line against the winner of Carlos Prates’ bout against Michael Morales at UFC 336 in January .
Former lightweight king Makhachev made the first defence of his welterweight title reign against Machado Garry in August Getty
Prates was originally expected to be the man to face Makhachev next after the Russian No. 1 pound-for-pound star defended his 170lbs throne against Ian Machado Garry in August.
However, Makhachev informed the UFC this month that he will not be ready for the Toronto card , despite suggesting after his win over Machado Garry that he wanted a quick turnaround.
Instead, Prates now fights Morales for the interim welterweight title at UFC 336, giving the winner a direct route to UFC gold.
Only time will tell when either welterweight star will get the chance to face Makhachev.

But the 35-year-old has said the unification fight will be one of his last.
“My next fight is one of the last in my career,” Makhachev said out of nowhere on social media on Friday.
“They say Prates is too dangerous for me and Morales is too good for me.
“So I want to face the best of them and prove to the world once again who is the best in the world.”
Makhachev dismissed retirement talk in August
Makhachev has already faced retirement questions this year.
Many MMA fans believed the two-division champion would call it quits after he fought Machado Garry at UFC 330.
Makhachev said he wants to ‘beat all records’ when asked about retiring this summer Getty
“Somebody put out fake news that I’m gonna retire after this fight,” Makhachev said in response to those rumours ahead of his victory.

“You’re never gonna find something like this outside the sport. I want to keep fighting, and we will beat all records and stay here for more years.”
This came at a time when Makhachev revealed he had been offered a deal with Zuffa Boxing by Saudi string-puller Turki Alalshikh.
Makhachev said he held ‘good talks’ with Alalshikh about a boxing match for the promotion, which was co-founded by UFC CEO Dana White .
A seemingly frustrated White discussed Makhachev’s UFC 336 absence this past weekend.
Makhachev is the protege of MMA legend Khabib Nurmagomedov, who retired prematurely in 2020 Getty
“On average, Islam fights like once a year,” White remarked.
“He was slated for January and then said, ‘I don’t want to fight until Ramadan.’
“You just can’t hold up divisions like this. You gotta keep moving. This fight [Prates vs Morales] makes sense.”
Makhachev broke Anderson Silva’s 16-fight record for the longest win streak in UFC history when he outpointed Machado Garry.

articles.headline: Russia shuts down last independent newspaper
keyFacts: Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced it is permanently shutting down due to pressure from state authorities.
Editor-in-Chief Sergei Sokolov stated authorities and intelligence services forced operations to end after office raids and revoked licenses.
The newspaper will shut down its servers and leave its office on November 9, Sokolov said.
body: Novaya Gazeta, Russia’s last independent newspaper and one of its most well-known, announced on Friday that it was shutting down for good.

Novaya Gazeta was founded in 1993, with former Soviet Premier Mikhail Gorbachev using the money from his Nobel Peace Prize to help set it up. In the over 30 years since, it has become a staple of independent Russian journalism, constantly at odds with authorities and frequently weathering censorship and harassment. On Friday, Editor-in-Chief Sergei Sokolov announced that the newspaper would be shutting down for good due to pressure from authorities, dramatically beginning his statement with, “We were killed.”

“On November 9th, we’ll turn off the lights in our home, where we’ve lived for 30 years, shut down the servers, and leave,” he said. “The newspaper is gone. The Russian authorities and Russian intelligence services forced the editorial staff to cease operations.
“Thirty-odd years of life together with the country and its citizens will end for us on the streets, without means of subsistence, under the constant threat of repression,” Sokolov added.

The outlet had long been under pressure, but state pressure escalated after the beginning of the war in Ukraine, when its reporting became viewed as actively seditious. Its print and online licenses were revoked within the year, forcing it to publish only online without registration. Earlier this month, security officers raided the newspaper’s office on Potapovsky Lane in central Moscow, and soon after it was evicted altogether.
In an interview with the fellow dissident outlet Meduza , which had fled Russia years before, Sokolov said the decision was made jointly by the staff after weighing all the factors.

“The circumstances are very simple. We got together, weighed all the factors, and made the decision as a group,” he said. “We don’t make decisions in secret — it was all done openly. When the online publication Novaya Gazeta was labeled a ‘foreign agent,’ we knew perfectly well this might come up.

“Even then, we said [among ourselves] that if the state escalated things any further, we wouldn’t survive,” Sokolov said. “That’s what happened — they took away our office and our means of supporting ourselves. And we didn’t survive. After that, it became impossible to work.”

Novaya Gazeta had made its name with its investigations, which frequently earned the ire of authorities. Six of its reporters have been killed since it began publication, which supporters believe was done on behalf of the Kremlin.
Russia’s nationalist Telegram community, known as milbloggers, were ecstatic over the closing, bemoaning that it hadn’t been done sooner.
LONGTIME SERBIAN LEADER VUCIC’S DEFEAT AT THE HANDS OF STUDENT MOVEMENT LEAVES WASHINGTON IN AWKWARD POSITION

“Under the guise of ‘honest journalism,’ and the protection of human rights, they systematically promoted the Western agenda, systematically discredited the army, reveled in any difficulties faced by the state, and promoted anti-Russian narratives,” an analysis republished by one of the most popular and influential milbloggers, Rybar, read. “What the editorial staff called ‘living with the country’ was, in reality, a continuous information operation, for which its chief ideologue, Dmitry Muratov, even received a token Nobel Prize from its curators.”

“The pompous lamentations about being ‘killed’ are aimed at a sympathetic audience, but the reality is much more prosaic — the tool has clearly served its purpose and will be replaced,” it reads, adding that “the factory of Russophobic content” will continue to operate by different means.”

articles.headline: They strangled us, says founder of Russian newspaper shut under pressure from authorities
keyFacts: Novaya Gazeta is shutting down and facing eviction after Russian authorities revoked its media license and blocked donations, staff said.
Co-founder Dmitry Muratov accused Russian authorities of forcing the thirty-year-old investigative newspaper to close through coordinated political repression.
Muratov said he does not know what will happen next, but stated they will do everything to stay true to their values.
body: - Published
At the editorial offices of Novaya Gazeta, they are packing up and shutting down.
Everywhere I look there are cardboard boxes and plastic bags. Everything must go.
For thirty years this has been Russia's most prominent independent newspaper, featuring investigative journalism fiercely critical of those in power.
Now Novaya Gazeta is being evicted from its home of three decades. The paper also says it's been blocked from receiving donations.
It's accusing the Russian authorities of killing it off.
"There are different ways to commit murder," journalist and co-founder of the paper Dmitry Muratov tells me. "They chose to strangle us."
"First, they blocked our websites and banned the paper edition. Then they revoked our media licence. One by one we were declared 'foreign agents', and our journalists were attacked.
"Now we can't earn any more money. The banks are refusing to accept donations from our readers. In our country there are political repressions going on. Those have reached us."
In 2021, Muratov was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for efforts "to safeguard freedom of expression, a precondition for democracy and lasting peace".
The award didn't stop the Russian authorities from designating him a 'foreign agent' in 2023. The label is often used to punish critics of the government.

Over the years Novaya Gazeta had developed a reputation for fearless investigative reporting on subjects such as corruption, human rights violations and abuse of power by officials and bureaucrats - dangerous topics in Russia.

The paper says that six colleagues were killed for "fulfilling their professional and civic duty". Those journalists include Anna Politkovskaya, who was shot dead in the stairwell of her apartment block twenty years ago this month. She had written extensively on the wars in Chechnya.

As I walk down a corridor, I spot the office Anna had used. Following her killing, the room and all the items in it were preserved and became a museum in her memory. Since the eviction order, most of the objects have already been removed. All that's left is the desk and, lying on top, a portrait of Anna.
In a statement on its website announcing the closure, Novaya Gazeta launched a stinging attack on the Russian authorities.
"They've killed us," it starts. "The newspaper is no more. The Russian authorities and Russian special services have forced the paper to stop its work."
The publication claims it is the victim of "a coordinated act" and blames "the repressive state apparatus".

"Human rights and freedoms have been eliminated in the country and their protection has been equated to a crimeâ¦ The courts have been destroyed along with the law. Having personal convictions is now state treason."
Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the pressure on independent journalism and independent Russian journalists has been growing.
Soon after the start of what the Kremlin calls the 'special military operation', new laws were adopted in Russia. Their aim: to punish dissent and silence criticism of the war and of those in power.

Earlier this year there was a police search of Novaya Gazeta's editorial office. A veteran investigative journalist Oleg Roldugin was arrested and charged with "unlawful access to computerised information".
In connection with the case the newspaper's current editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov was recently taken in for police questioning and his home was searched.

Despite increasing pressure, Novaya Gazeta managed to continue operating, albeit in a reduced form. Loyal readers used VPNs, virtual private networks, to circumvent official blocking of the website. But the loss of its licence and other restrictions were a major blow to the publication.
How does Dmitry Muratov view the future?

"We are in the middle of a terrible catastrophe," Mr Muratov tells me. "Different dictatorships in the world seek chaos. They use chaos to rule their countries and peoples and to strengthen their personal power.
"I don't know what will happen next. I do know that we will do everything to stay true to our values: the human right to life. Human rights override the rights of states."
Novaya Gazeta's demise is very much the end of an era.
In an increasingly authoritarian Russia, it's also a sign of the times.

articles.headline: Pope Leo becomes first pontiff to vote in a U.S. election
keyFacts: The Vatican confirmed that Pope Leo became the first pontiff to vote in a U.S. election by submitting a mail-in ballot.

Pope Leo is moving ahead to South America next month after recovering and resuming his activities at the Vatican.
body: has become the first pontiff to vote in a U.S. election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the American-born pope submitted a mail-in ballot in ahead of November's midterm elections, citing his longstanding belief in civic participation.
The pope, formerly Cardinal , "has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so," the Holy See press office said.
"The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes," the Vatican said in a statement.
The Will County Clerk's Office confirmed to CBS News that he is on the list of voters who requested a mail-in ballot, with a registered address in New Lenox.

The Chicago Sun-Times first reported Leo's vote and quoted the chief of staff at the Will County Clerk's Office as saying the pope requested a mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. This was just days before his .
The pope has been recovering and resuming his activities at the Vatican after and is moving ahead with to South America next month.
Last month, Leo told a general audience at the Vatican that the faithful should leave behind "all passivity and indifference" toward current events.

"We cannot remain as unengaged spectators; rather, we must listen with our hearts, allow ourselves to be challenged, and become involved," the pope said on Sept. 2 in St. Peter's Square, according to the Catholic News Service. "With Christ and sustained by the power of his Spirit, believers are called to take on the burdens of their brothers and sisters, especially those who are crushed by injustice, discrimination and violence."

The pope has a long history of civic engagement in the U.S., the Vatican said, confirming that during his nearly two decades as a missionary then bishop in Peru, Leo voted whenever he was eligible. He holds U.S. and Peruvian citizenship.

According to records from the Illinois State Board of Elections, the pope, as Robert Prevost, was registered to vote in Cook County. The Associated Press reports he previously voted in five primary elections since 2000 — on the Democratic ballots in 2008 and 2019 and Republican ballots in 2012, 2014 and 2016.
Illinois has closed primaries, which means voters must declare a party preference to receive a ballot. No such declaration is required in general elections.
The pope submitted ballots in every general election since 2000, except in 2020 and 2022, the AP reported, citing Illinois election records.

articles.headline: AI-powered game development is 'leading to an explosion of content,' Roblox says, as it brags about 70,000 games published on its platform in the last 5 months alone
keyFacts: Roblox announced in its Q3 shareholder letter that users have published over 70,000 games using its new AI-powered Build tool.
Roblox stated that AI adoption is leading to an explosion of content and dramatically compressing the time needed to create playable games.
Roblox launched new initiatives called Roblox Everywhere and the Universal Player to import external games into the Roblox cloud using AI.
body: Valve recently admitted that it has a problem with AI slop games and clones flooding Steam—it doesn't know what to do about it just yet, but it at least acknowledges that it's an issue. Now we have Roblox, speaking from the other side of that coin in its Q3 2026 shareholder letter, in which it bragged that the July release of Build, its AI-powered "prompt-to-game creation tool," users have published more than 70,000 games.

"During the last three months, we have witnessed an inflection point in AI adoption and content generation in the gaming industry overall, and on Roblox in particular," the letter states. "AI-enabled game creation, automation in code generation and AI supported asset creation are leading to an explosion of content. The time it takes to go from an idea to a playable game is compressing dramatically, and so is the time it takes to adapt a game for new devices."

The "explosion of content" remark is what jumps out at me first and foremost. Is that really a good thing—content, in explosive quantities? That is essentially what Valve is facing on Steam that's widely considered a problem—an ever-growing mountain of content—yet in the world of Roblox, it's a feature, not a bug. And Roblox is not looking to stem the tide.

"We have been embracing AI to accelerate creation since the first release of Roblox Studio Assistant in December 2023," the letter continues. "Over the past month, more than 80% of the top 100 games on Roblox (ranked by hours engaged) used AI tools to accelerate creation, and the number of daily asset uploads to the Roblox cloud tripled month-over-month.

"Since Q2, time spent using AI tools (including Build, Studio Assistant, and external AI via MCP) tripled among our top creators, and those using our MCP server daily grew nearly 5x. In Q3, Break and Steal an Egg and Huss Valley were both created almost entirely with AI and both broke into the Roblox top 20 (ranked by concurrent players). Build is our new prompt-to-game creation tool. Since its alpha launch in New Zealand, Singapore, Serbia and Thailand, more than 500,000 users have used Build—and have published over 70,000 games."

Take a moment to think about that: Build launched in July, five months ago, which means we're looking at a rough average of 14,000 games per month. And that's with Build still not fully launched yet, so only a fairly small portion of the Roblox userbase has access to it. I can't help but wonder, with a certain sense of alarm, what will happen when the doors are opened to more populous parts of the world.

Roblox, however, says it is "uniquely positioned to capture this moment," which is seeing "traditional barriers to software and content creation" giving way to a focus on "distribution, audience aggregation, monetization, discovery, and safety."
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

To further capitalize on that, Roblox has kicked off two new initiatives: Roblox Everywhere, revealed in September as a way to make Roblox games playable outside of the Roblox platform, and the Universal Player, which is basically the reverse of that: "AI is used to seamlessly import any existing game into the Roblox cloud platform while transforming it to run multiplayer, on any device (at the upper edge of the device's performance capabilities), with instant join, instant UGC updates, local 3D, and access to Roblox services for discovery, safety, communication, and monetization."

That's interesting: Details are scant but the idea seems to be to make Roblox a platform for all game developers, akin to Steam, GOG, or the PlayStation Store, with minimal fuss or muss: Just make your game, then zippity-pow it through the AI machine, and suddenly you've got a full-on Roblox game and access to a massive audience that previously would've been much more of a headache to reach. And Roblox gets basically the same: Its goal "is to capture 10% of the global gaming market and an even greater share in the US."

"As content becomes abundant, attention and connection become scarce," the letter says, extolling the virtues of Roblox's platform. "What sets our distribution apart is that it runs on social connections: people come to Roblox to play with their friends, so every new game can reach players through an existing social graph, through friends inviting friends, and through social influencers, which we believe enables great content to find its ideal audience faster than on any other platform."

Maybe Roblox is right. Hell, maybe EA chief Andrew Wilson was right—maybe the future really is all about billions of people cranking out content while corporations fight over where to put it all. It's hard to argue that Roblox hasn't put up serious shareholder value so far, after all, and while Steam doesn't have shareholders it's still making bank, AI slop problem or no. Still, I can't say that making speed and quantity the key indicators of success really represents the kind of future for videogaming that I'd like.

articles.headline: Thunder reportedly sign ex-Raptors former first-rounder amid Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace injuries
keyFacts: Thunder guards Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace will undergo surgery for long-term injuries and miss several months, general manager Sam Presti announced.
The Thunder plan to sign former first-round draft pick Ochai Agbaji to add backcourt depth following the injuries, according to league sources reported by HoopsHype.
Agbaji's signing gives him an opportunity to prove he belongs in the NBA after previously playing for the Jazz, Raptors, Nets, and Knicks.
body: The Oklahoma City Thunder have been one of the best teams in the NBA over the last two seasons, and it doesn't look like that will change this season either. However, even though the season has only been underway for a little over a week, the team has already suffered some significant injuries.
Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace recently suffered injuries, and it was announced earlier in the week that both could potentially miss the remainder of the season.

“The Oklahoma City Thunder lost two starters to long-term injuries in their 108-101 win over the LA Clippers on Sunday night. General manager Sam Presti announced Monday that guard Jalen Williams will undergo surgery for a dislocated left ankle and fractured fibula, while guard Cason Wallace will undergo surgery for a torn labrum in his left shoulder. Both players are expected to miss several months,” ESPN wrote.
On Monday, Thunder general manager Sam Presti met with the media to discuss the injuries. When asked about potential roster additions, he didn't have an answer just yet.

“I haven't thought about anything relative to the roster spot,” Presti said. “I understand the question. But all I'm really focused on right now is players, giving them the right support and then helping everybody in our group realize that we have a tremendous challenge in front of us.”

A few days later, it looks like Presti has a better idea of which direction he wants to go in the backcourt. The Thunder are signing former first-round pick Ochai Agbaji, who played college basketball at Kansas.

“The Oklahoma City Thunder plan to sign Ochai Agbaji, league sources told hoopshype. Agbaji has averaged 7.2 points in four NBA seasons with the Utah Jazz, Toronto Raptors, and Brooklyn Nets. Agbaji was most recently with the New York Knicks in training camp,” HoopsHype’s Michael Scott wrote.

Adding Agbaji gives OKC another option for its backcourt and provides some much-needed depth. The Thunder are typically smart about the players they add to their roster, so they clearly see something in the former Toronto Raptors guard.
There are several ways Agbaji could impact a game for OKC. This is a real opportunity for him to prove that he still belongs in the NBA after being cut by the New York Knicks during the preseason.

articles.headline: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
keyFacts: The United States scrapped the G20 foreign ministers' group photo after European officials refused to be pictured alongside Russia's Sergey Lavrov.
The G20 foreign ministers meeting exposed deep rifts among member nations over the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
A diplomatic source said no joint statement is expected, and Washington will publish a chair's summary instead.
body: The United States has scrapped a traditional group photo of foreign ministers after European officials refused to be pictured alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.

The move exposes deep rifts at the heart of the Group of 20 (G20), whose foreign ministers are meeting in the southern city of Atlanta in the United States for talks overshadowed by the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
“There will be no family photo featuring our European partners together with Mr Lavrov,” German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said, according to the dpa news agency.

Lavrov, who remains under Western sanctions imposed after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, arrived in Atlanta ahead of the talks, Russian state media reported. Moscow said on Thursday that he would use his speech to argue against international sanctions. Ukraine was not invited, the Abu Dhabi-based newspaper The National reported.
A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Russia’s presence at the G20 “in no way legitimises its actions”.

The European Union’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas pledged on Thursday to urge G20 partners to strengthen support for Ukraine and pursue accountability through a special tribunal and claims commission, after a Russian strike on a Ukrainian railway station killed at least 14 people earlier that day.
The meeting also comes weeks after US President Donald Trump issued sanctions waivers allowing Russia to export diesel to ease fuel prices before the November 3 midterm elections.

Opening the talks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged members to cooperate on economic and geopolitical crises threatening global trade, energy and food supplies, and freedom of navigation, dpa reported. Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz after US-Israeli strikes began in late February, and global energy prices have risen sharply since.
“Both maritime and food security drive economic security,” Rubio wrote on X.

No joint statement is expected. A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Washington will instead publish a chair’s summary it has drafted. The source added: “The G20 is no longer really a forum where foreign ministers can reach agreement on a statement.”
No government has said whether Rubio and Lavrov will hold a formal bilateral meeting.

China sent Executive Vice Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu in place of Foreign Minister Wang Yi, according to a delegation list released by the Department of State. South Africa, a founding G20 member, has been excluded by Washington, and the African Union is represented by Burundi’s Edouard Bizimana.
The Atlanta talks are the last ministerial meeting of the US G20 presidency before leaders meet in Miami on December 14 and 15.

articles.headline: Warframe's fantasy-pilled sister Soulframe finally goes open to all this November, though Digital Extremes are "nervous" about certain changes
keyFacts: Digital Extremes announced that the fantasy RPG Soulframe will become available to everyone on November 6th after two years in closed alpha.
The upcoming open prelude update introduces a region purging system and a directed mission structure to help players avoid getting lost.
Creative director Geoff Crookes and lead designer Scott McGregor stated they are nervous about the changes potentially disrupting the game's cosy ambience.
body: Warframe creators Digital Extremes have announced that their free-to-play fantasy RPG Soulframe will be available for everyone to download on 6th November, after two years in closed alpha. Finally, you serfs without "prelude" keys will be able to fire up Soulframe.com and make sense of my ranting about the sleeping animals on the lobby screen.

The new "open prelude" will land shortly before the game's 17th major update, Verse of the Veilands, which lets you grow your Omen wolfpup allies into rideable adult wolves by finding the ingredients for a special biscuit. More importantly, prelude 17 violently rearranges the game's wistful world, adding an Ubisoft-esque region purging system that is designed to guide new players a bit more emphatically towards the game's "votives". Aka, missions. Yes, Digital Extremes sort of have a bespoke term for every game feature in Soulframe. I find this can be either charming or maddening, depending on how much sleep I've had.

Here's how the region purging will work: after completing the game's Tormented Stag quest, you'll find that the landscape is being corrupted by siphons deployed by the villainous star-faring Ode faction. You have to complete votives to build energy and learn the sacred song of each region, allowing you to cleanse it and restore the environment.

In a roundtable preview session last week, creative director Geoff Crookes and lead designer Scott McGregor expressed a certain amount of anxiety about deliberately polluting Soulframe's fairytale ambience. "Scott and I were just talking yesterday about, aesthetically, how nervous we are about this change," Crookes commented, "because the game has gotten a lot of really great feedback on how cosy it is, how beautiful the world is, and you're going to enter a game that is much more unforgiving and harsh at first glance."

That said, he thinks the shift "pairs really well with going into open alpha, because it is a much stronger breadcrumb [trail] for the player, to pull them into the world and give them a bit more ownership of what they're doing." Once rinsed of Ode siphons, regions will appear more like how they are in previous versions of Soulframe, with activities such as fishing and new resources to snaffle.

McGregor added that hitherto, a lot of Soulframe players have gotten lost and put the game down after completing the opening "Fables", or story quests. "It's a really big change to the structural flow of the game, you know," he told the assembled journorabble. "We're very open and discoverable, and we had a lot of player feedback that was basically 'what do I do next? What do I do next? I don't know what to do next'.

"So [it's] taking that and mashing it with the votive system, which is our mission system for the game, and making that more of a directed experience," he went on, "and then once they get through that directed experience, they can go back to that open world." Prelude 17 will also let you accept votives more straightforwardly from the world map, after finding the local representative or mission giver.

Digital Extremes have a new Soulframe "pact" or character loadout on the boil, the Ode Shrike. It's a dastardly poacher class who specialises in spike traps and throwable bolas. The Shrike's standout ability is a balloon dart that lets you hoist enemies into the sky, as in Metal Gear Solid V.

You can read more about Soulframe's on-going reinventions on the official site. While you won't need a key to get access as of Nov 6th, the game's paid Founders program will remain the same. Digital Extremes will likely still run closed preview builds alongside the "open prelude", testing out features with a smaller group of players. They're also looking into giving you the ability to reset your character, so you can check out any new material added to parts of the game you've finished.

I'm not sure I've ever been exhilarated by Soulframe, but I like the poise, flamboyance and gentle complexity of its combat. I also really enjoy its faded tapestry aesthetics, though I think it's yanking on the goo-goo glands too avidly with all these fluffy forest animals. Enough photogenic wolfpups, Digital Extremes - let's see you make, I don't know, a blobfish look adorable.

It's also very interesting as a new live service project from a company defined by the success of Warframe. I spoke to the Soulframe developers earlier in the year about the challenge of borrowing Warframe's thunder without getting lost in its shadow.
Read this next

- Soulframe's latest major update is a broadside of pirate weapons, class abilities and outfits, plus falling alien skytowers
- I love fantasy RPG Soulframe’s cosy start screen even though it could be a creepy piece of habit-forming design
