articles.headline: Manchester United stick with Michael Carrick ahead of Chelsea matchup as dressing-room discord fuels crisis
keyFacts: Michael Carrick will remain manager of Manchester United for their upcoming match against Chelsea on Saturday despite an eight-game winless run.
Manchester United players have publicly criticized the club's ambition and tactics during this poor run of form, according to the article.
Coach Michael Carrick stated that Bruno Fernandes will retain his captaincy after being benched following a public questioning of team tactics.
body: To the surprise of many, Michael Carrick will continue to be in the dugout for Manchester United as they face Chelsea on Saturday. During their eight-game winless run in all competitions, United have allowed 15 goals while scoring six, and off the pitch, everything is unraveling, with players and fans alike questioning the direction of the club. United have been in this position before, and it has usually led to a change of manager and a rebuild of the club from the ground up.

But what's different is that during this rut, players are publicly speaking out. While things will sometimes leak via undisclosed sources, players saying the quiet part out loud about what's going on with the club is not a good look.  about the need for the club to have higher standards and claimed that it's lacking ambition after a poor loss to Atletico Madrid in Champions League play, but it went from bad to worse as captain  after a humbling loss to Como, questioning the team's tactics.
How to watch Chelsea vs. Manchester United, odds
Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 8:30 a.m. ET
Location: Stamford Bridge  -- London
TV: USA Network
Odds: Chelsea -105; Draw +270; Manchester United +270

That led to Fernandes being benched and United failing yet again to pick up a victory. While the public view is that Fernandes will retain his captaincy, the episode has to strip away at least some of Carrick's authority within the club.

"There is no decision to be made on [the captaincy]," Carrick said. "It will be Bruno. Listen, we're clear with the situation of the team and as a football club at the moment. He's an important player for this group. He has been and he will be."

Ahead of a match where both teams are struggling, the slightest lack of balance could lead to yet another United loss. With no clear sign that authority lies with the manager rather than the captain, especially after Carrick held meetings about the future of his job, this could get worse before it gets better.

What do you do if United concede an early goal and the match goes off the rails? On the evidence we've seen, it's tough to say Carrick will be able to get the club out of that spiral, and if he can't, there's no reason why he should be the manager. On paper, while too much money was invested in the midfield instead of defense, this isn't a bad squad, but United find themselves in the relegation race only one season after qualifying for Champions League play. Even their numbers scream midtable, not doomed to relegation.

That's where the mentality of the squad comes in. It's been a persistent issue since Sir Alex Ferguson left, and it's not an issue that seems to be going away anytime soon. At times, it will lie dormant for a season during which you think United are righting the ship, only to come back at the worst time possible. Carrick is only a symptom of a larger issue at Manchester United, and the club has gone through eight permanent managers since Ferguson without sustained success. It's not for lack of spending, and even though there are questions around who is recruited, for the most part, the squads have been fine. They just can never perform to the sum of their parts.

Since Jim Ratcliffe took over, the club has been more focused on profits off the pitch than actual success on it, and that's catching up with United. Turning that around is going to be quite a challenge. Fan protests have been seen, but they aren't igniting real change, and we may be in a situation where United need a sustained spell in the bottom half of the table to lead to anything different. In short, this is already dire, and every day with Carrick at the helm delays the start of that turnaround, even if that isn't his fault. United have become a club without a direction, and that's something Chelsea can take advantage of as the Xabi Alonso era at Stamford Bridge has signs of success but needs a result to get back on the right track.

articles.headline: Meta settles another social media addiction case just before trial
keyFacts: Meta settled a social media addiction lawsuit brought by an 18-year-old woman from Mississippi just before a trial was set to begin.
The plaintiff's lawyer announced the settlement on Friday, following earlier settlements with TikTok and YouTube, with terms remaining undisclosed.
Snap is now the sole remaining defendant in the case, and CEO Evan Spiegel is expected to testify during the upcoming trial.
body: Meta settles another social media addiction case just before trial
Snap is now the only defendant in the case.

Meta has reached a settlement in another social media addiction lawsuit in a move that will allow it to avoid a trial that was set to kick off next month. Snap is now the only defendant in the case, which is one of several closely watched lawsuits against social media platforms.

The lawsuit was brought by an 18-year-old woman from Mississippi known as K.D.B who, according to Reuters, has "described staying awake for hours scrolling social media, losing focus in class and engaging in self-harm using methods shown in social media videos." Jury selection kicked off earlier this week in Los Angeles.

On Friday, K.D.B's lawyer announced that she had reached a settlement with Meta after previously settling with TikTok and YouTube. "We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client," attorney Emily Jeffcott said in a statement.
Terms of the settlement weren't disclosed and Meta didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Now, Snap is the only remaining defendant in the case. CEO Evan Spiegel is expected to testify in the trial that could last several weeks. If he does take the stand, it will be the first time the Snap founder has appeared in a social media addiction trial. Snap previously settled in another high-profile case involving similar claims. A jury later ruled against Meta and YouTube in the trial and the two were ordered to pay $6 million in damages.

In a statement, a Snap spokesperson didn't comment on Meta's settlement, but said the lawsuit "fundamentally misrepresent(s)" how Snapchat works. "From the beginning, Snapchat was built differently from traditional social media: it opens to a camera, not a feed, not a ranking of what other people post or other social comparison metrics," the spokesperson said. "We have built safeguards into the platform, introduced safety tools and educational resources, and we believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs' experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed."

Meta and Snap have both faced a flood of lawsuits over alleged safety lapses and social media addiction. Snap also recently settled a long-running lawsuit over its "speed filter," which is alleged to have played a role in several high-speed car crashes involving teens.

articles.headline: High Stakes, Higher Boots: Here Are Horror Games’ Best-Dressed Women
keyFacts: A GameSpot article ranked the eight best-dressed female protagonists in horror games based on distinctiveness and influence.
The rankings feature characters from major and cult titles like Silent Hill 3, Resident Evil 4, and Fatal Frame.
The author stated that horror-game fashion serves as a uniform uniting female fans in both pain and resilience.
body: While the female horror-game protagonist fends off demons and other predators, she is also serving looks . This is the rose-covered cross women are made to bear: We must inspire others with our appearance even while covered in gore. Within the broader scope of patriarchal society, this expectation, which then bleeds into fashionable horror games like Silent Hill 3 and the Fatal Frame series, is unfair. Women actively experiencing horror-game scenarios (a hateful god in Silent Hill 3, homicidal spirits in Fatal Frame, etc.) are already dealing with the stress of needing to do things like craft bullets and practice healthy inventory management. It seems cruel for developers to make them think about how their knee-high socks are rolling down mid-duel, too.

But for women like me, who love horror games as much as they appreciate clean drinking water, horror-game protagonist fashion is also a uniform we can use to show we're united--both in our pain and in our resilience. Anyway, it takes a bold personality to make sure your hair is brushed and blouse is buttoned before steel-piping an enemy into dust. So I've collected eight of the best female horror-game protagonist outfits across major games like Resident Evil 4 and cult-favorites like Koudelka , ranked based on distinctiveness and influence. This is not a place for practicality.
8. Koudelka Iasant, Koudelka (2000)

The psychic Koudelka had incredible fashion foresight: Her horror RPG takes place in a monastery in 1898, but she's wearing the perfect amount of polyester lace for a goth club in the '90s. This asynchronicity is just one of the many awkward details that stopped Koudelka from becoming a big deal at launch (GameSpot's Koudelka review from 2000 complains of "lackluster gameplay"), but it's also what makes her outfit special. Koudelka wears a jean skirt so short that her Victoria's Secret panties peek out like a ghost, plus a see-through black corset and brassy bangles that drunkenly gesture at her 19th-century setting. She's a witch, and confidently so.
7. Jessica Riley, Until Dawn (2015)

Until Dawn is one of the best horror games of the PS4 generation, though its middling 2024 remake and unpopular 2025 movie adaptation has since rusted its reputation. But the appeal of fan-favorite Jess has always been as clean as coal. She wears her winter coat with its faux-fur collar popped out like a lion's mane, as bitchy as possible, and has her low-rise skinny jeans just high enough on her sharp hips to be practical. Like Jess herself, the outfit is smug in how overly trendy it is. But a woman with a little ego is nonetheless something to admire .
6. Fiona Belli, Haunting Ground (2005)

Fiona was misunderstood for a long time, both by Haunting Ground 's initial audience and the demented men in the game, who chase her around her own family's castle trying to get her pregnant . But, among new fans who have discovered Haunting Ground 20 years later, Fiona's outfit has finally earned her empathy--and respect.

Her captor forces her to wear what is now seen as the prototypical horror-game protagonist armor in tall leather boots, a short skirt, and a medieval-inspired blouse that reveals her delicate waist and the more vulnerable organs. Her top includes corset lacing on the back using a powder blue ribbon, nearly the same color as the gleaming stone set in the bodice of the blouse and Fiona's light eyes. But they are brighter than the stone, which she hasn't chosen for herself.
5. Alice Liddell, Alice: Madness Returns (2011)

Developer American McGee's Alice: Madness Returns seems to have become more popular each year since publisher EA rejected plans for a sequel , and part of that frenzy is motivated by Alice's singed-effigy look. There are parts of her appearance that are unreplicable, like the glare in her olive eyes and the permanent, unhappy curve of her mouth.

But her blood-speckled tea dress, the petticoat under her gown, and dirty apron on top of it remind me of the invigorating Japanese Lolita fashion subculture. This fashion style uses frilly, dolly dresses and ribbons to accentuate the truth of the woman that wears them: Her mouth is unhappy like Alice's. She's using her dress-code-appropriate skirt length to question why she's ever been told to wear something more revealing, like Fiona. Instead, the unbelievable height of Alice's buckled platform boots suggest you will die before you see what's under that skirt.
4. Maria, Silent Hill 2 (2001)

Opposite to Alice, the mysterious dream girl Maria uses her body as a lure. Her outfit has been replicated by fans for decades (though it originated in a Christina Aguilera red carpet look , which Konami devs decided to borrow), but it requires unique nakedness of both the soul and body: Unlike other horror game protagonists, Maria ditches socks completely. Her knees are bare, a mulberry cardigan squeezes around her chest, and her midriff is also exposed, save for the soaring butterfly tattoo on her hip. As most outfits featuring a pink cheetah-print skirt tend to be, it's memorable and good motivation for being daring within your closet--though Maria, the ghost, hides behind the feeling.
3. Ashley Graham, Resident Evil 4 (2005)

Big, brown leather boots. Skirt that ends at the thigh, a tight sweater vest that's perfect for the apple-crisp middle of October. Ashley looks like the standard horror-game protagonist, but that's because the plucky president's daughter helped define it. Developer Capcom established modern survival-horror gameplay with its mega-influential shooter Resident Evil 4--and the successful 2023 remake reminded everyone of that fact--but Ashley handled the style.

Her outfit is that of a mature schoolgirl, reflecting both the college-campus chic seen in contemporary horror films like Urban Legend (1998) and Scream 3 (2000), as well her cloistered upbringing. Ashley is ultimately an unwilling victim, but not when it comes to fashion. She probably smells like Marc Jacobs and a drop of nervous sweat.
2. Heather Mason, Silent Hill 3 (2003)

I have an unfounded theory that Heather Mason's outfit--forest green cargo skirt, Scooby Doo orange sweater vest, and those classic horror girl brown boots--might have inspired Ashley's matching color palette, which is why I've ranked her outfit slightly higher for originality. Heather also means something different when she wears her elevated schoolgirl look; Ashley's wealth makes her seem glamorous, but also naive. Heather, instead, is a one-bedroom realist. She has high endurance, though she'd prefer the cult that raised her to stop trying to use her womb to grow evil God . Within the chaos, her simple autumn outfit and practical puffer vest--with pockets!--remind her and fans who relate, she's a regular girl who can handle what she must.
1. Fatal Frame: Mask of the Lunar Eclipse remake (2023)

Ultimately, when a girl these days talks about a "horror-game protagonist outfit," she's likely referring to Fatal Frame: Mask of the Lunar Eclipse from 2023, specifically. Koei Tecmo's remake finally freed its formerly Japan-exclusive Wii horror game after 15 years, and a new generation of stylish women have now met the spiritually tortured protagonists Misaki, Ruka, Madoka. The girls are saturated in death--poltergeists eat the cursed island they've been foolish to return to--but they are also caught up on Japanese mall fashion. Their outfits include the knee-high socks and microskirts, as required by the women of horror before them, but also more embroidery, chiffon bows, and milk froth-like dresses than ever before, fitting in perfectly with the Y2K nostalgia of other 2026 fashion trends.

Fatal Frame just adds a bloody border to the decade's classic silhouette: its fitted tops, bottoms, and airy cardigans. Fans of the fashion online and vintage resale sites recommend 2000's J-fashion brands like Axes Femme to get the delicate look, which is the best example of how your soul and your clothes touch with soft cotton hands.

articles.headline: What Are Open-Weight AI Models?
keyFacts: An open-weight model makes its trained neural network weights publicly available so users can download and run their own local copies.
Open-weight models differ from open-source models because publishing weights alone does not always meet the Open Source Initiative definition.
Developers have limited control once users download models, which allows independent researchers to examine models more closely and identify faults.
body: You might use a chatbot without thinking about who controls the model behind it. Then an update changes how it answers, or you want help with something private you’d rather keep on your computer.

An open-weight model lets you download the pretrained AI and run it yourself. You’ll need software to use it and a computer that can handle it, but you get to keep a working copy. While chatbots get most of the attention, image and video generators can also have open-weight options.

Downloading an AI model doesn’t necessarily give you unrestricted permission or reveal everything that went into making it, though. Sure, you get more autonomy in how you use AI, but the word “open” still leaves a lot unsaid. Here’s what open-weight models are, what you can do with them and what to consider before trying one for yourself.
More from CNET
What are open-weight models and how do they work?

In a chatbot, the AI model is the software that generates the answers. During training, the model learns patterns by adjusting billions of numerical values called neural network weights. When you ask a question, the model uses your prompt and those learned patterns to predict what text should come next, building its answer one piece at a time.

Developers of closed models, including those behind ChatGPT and Claude, keep their weights private. An open-weight model makes its trained weights publicly available. That means you can download them and run your own copy using compatible software.

“Whenever you open-weight a model, all the weights are all over the place on the internet, like on Hugging Face and other servers,” Pierre Stock, VP of science at AI company Mistral, tells CNET. “So it’s virtually impossible to cut access to this model.”
With a free model and app, you can chat locally without a subscription or usage fees. More importantly, a fully local setup also keeps your prompts and files off an AI provider’s servers.

Don’t worry if you’re not tech-savvy, because you won’t have to write code or open a terminal to do it. Desktop apps like LM Studio, Ollama and Jan let you download and run open-weight models with a simple install, giving you a ChatGPT-like interface right on your Mac or PC. You still need a computer that can handle your chosen model. Once everything is installed, you can keep chatting offline.
If you know how, you can also adapt the model through further training, where permitted by its license. You don’t have to train an entirely new model from scratch.
Open-weight vs. open-source

People often use these terms interchangeably, but they don’t mean quite the same thing. An open-weight model can also be open-source, but publishing the weights alone doesn’t qualify under the Open Source Initiative’s definition.

Developers must share the code used to train and run it. They must also provide enough information about the training data for a skilled person to build a model that works much the same way. The terms must allow people to use, study, change and share it.

Under the OSI definition, developers don’t have to share the data they used to train a model. The Free Software Foundation says that should be part of the deal, with users free to use and change the data themselves.

Some open-weight licenses limit business use, meaning a model might be free to download but off-limits for an app you want to sell. That kind of restriction would disqualify it under the OSI definition. An open-source license can still require you to keep the same terms when you share a version you’ve changed.
Which models have open weights?

Chinese models currently lead independent AI testing company Artificial Analysis’s intelligence rankings for open-weight models. You may already know about DeepSeek, but there is also Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 and Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 family, which offer downloadable weights.

Some US alternatives come from the companies behind familiar chatbots. OpenAI offers gpt-oss models separately from ChatGPT, while Google has Gemma models. Meta has Muse Glimmer and added Muse Spark Open alongside its Llama models, and Nvidia has Nemotron.

You don’t have to stick with the chatbot giants, either. A US-based startup, Reflection, released Beam, whose weights are now available to download. Another US startup, Thinking Machines Lab, offers its model Inkling.

Europe has a contender in France’s Mistral AI. Its downloadable models include Mistral Large 3 and the smaller Ministral 3 family. The newer Mistral Large 4, dubbed Le Chonk, is available now with downloadable weights.
Not every model mentioned here will run on a laptop. Some larger models need server hardware, while smaller versions can run on personal computers or even smaller devices, like phones.
What are the limits?

An open-weight model can still hallucinate when it’s running offline on your laptop. It can also carry biases from its training. Developers may publish weights while keeping training data private, leaving outsiders unable to fully check what went into them.
Performance varies by model and task, so openness alone won’t tell you whether it will beat a closed alternative.
The freedom to change a model also means people can weaken or remove its safeguards.

“Guardrails are necessary to open-weighting a model,” Stock says. When I ask how to keep them safe if people can remove those protections after downloading a model, Stock says, “With a lot of work, you can partially overcome the guardrails,” comparing the effort involved to do so to fine-tuning a model yourself.

Once people have downloaded copies, the original developer has limited control over what happens next. A company can cut off someone misusing its online service, and releasing a safer replacement won’t update everyone’s download.

Yet those same downloads allow independent researchers to examine models more closely and identify faults. Researchers can test changes themselves, rather than depend on the developer to investigate a complaint.

Microsoft and other companies cited that benefit in an open letter defending open weights after reports of potential US restrictions on Chinese models. They argued that keeping these tools available helps security teams defend against attackers using AI.
“When you open-weight a model, you’re essentially enabling the entire ecosystem to progress together,” Stock tells CNET.
Would an open-weight model be useful to you?

Open-weight models can draft emails, summarize documents, analyze local files and help with coding just like cloud models. However, when you run one locally, its speed and ability to handle long documents depend on both the model and your computer’s memory and processing power.
Larger models usually run more smoothly on computers with plenty of memory or a powerful GPU, like a Mac with 16GB or 36GB RAM, though smaller models may work on an 8GB Mac.

If you already own the necessary hardware, it’s worth considering installing an open-weight model. But if you have to buy a new computer to run them, weigh that cost against a $20-per-month subscription for a cloud model.

You can also use some open-weight models through their developers’ own websites that run them for you, like DeepSeek and Kimi. That’s less work than downloading and running the model yourself, but your prompts go to the provider.

If you want occasional help writing an email and don’t mind using an online service, a hosted chatbot may suit you just fine. ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude all have free plans, so avoiding a subscription doesn’t automatically require running your own AI.

Open weights give you the option to take more control yourself, not to mention keeping sensitive documents on your device. An assistant that keeps working when you don’t have access to the internet sounds great. So does being able to keep a model you like even after its developer retires the online one.
“You don’t want to live in a world in which someone can cut off access to your model,” Stock says.

The future also looks promising with open-weight models being installed on smaller devices. Google’s Gemma models include smaller versions for phones and laptops. Mistral has a similar range of models, including specialized ones intended for particular uses and devices.
“We also have models specialized in audio, for instance,” Stock says, “and those can fit literally on the smartwatch.”

articles.headline: Polish president scrambles back from overseas trip amid Donald Tusk-led ‘coup d’état’ at police-swarmed Constitutional Tribunal
keyFacts: Polish police raided the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw on Friday, putting up barriers and removing security amid a forced change of court leadership.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk defended the raid, stating that restoring the rule of law after years of Law and Justice party lawlessness required decisive action.
body: President Karol Nawrocki, Poland’s head of state aligned with the right-wing Law and Justice party (PiS), canceled a Friday trip to Senegal and is heading back to Warsaw amid what his allies are calling a “coup d’état.”

Metropolitan Police Headquarters announced Friday that its officers are “carrying out statutory activities at the premises of the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw” — the nation’s highest court. Authorities have removed security from the premises and put up barriers around the area as they attempt to restore “public order” amid a forced change of leadership.
“At such a moment, the President must be in Poland. I’m interrupting my flight to Senegal. I’m returning,” Nawrocki wrote on social media.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk, a bitter political adversary of Nawrocki and the Constitutional Tribunal, took credit for the raid and said it was necessary to prevent lawlessness.

Police officers stand behind the fence with a rosary hanging on it as protesters gather outside the headquarters of Poland’s Constitutional Court in Warsaw after police blocked access to the court building on Oct. 30, 2026. (Wojtek Radwanski/AFP via Getty Images)

“Restoring the rule of law is our duty,” Tusk announced late Friday . “After years of PiS-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way.”

Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska , the longest-tenured judge on the Constitutional Tribunal, has been appointed interim president after the removal of court president Bogdan Swieczkowski. This was reflected on the court’s website.

However, the Constitutional Tribunal’s account on social media platform X issued a contradictory statement : “An unlawful takeover of the Constitutional Tribunal’s website has occurred. The President of [the Constitutional Tribunal] remains Bogdan Święczkowski, and the Vice-President is Bartłomiej Sochański. Ms. Anna Korwin-Piotrowska is not a judge of the Constitutional Tribunal. All persons participating in these actions are committing the crime of a coup d’état.”
At the center of the dispute is the appointment of a new judge to the tribunal, Maciej Berek, who was elected for the position by the left-controlled lower chamber of parliament.

PiS has questioned whether Berek’s career technically meets the requirement for judges to have 10 years’ experience as a legal adviser. The left wing has pushed back on this, and a war over definitions has developed.

President of Poland Karol Nawrocki attends a group photo during the 20th informal meeting of the Arraiolos Group Heads of State in Tallinn, Estonia, Friday, Oct. 10, 2025. (Sergei Grits/AP Photo, File)

Berek is required to swear an oath of office in front of Nawrocki, but the president has dodged any meeting that would allow such an oath to happen. The new judge previously tried to sign an oath addressed to Nawrocki as a substitute, but the Constitutional Tribunal — which is ideologically aligned with PiS — rejected the gesture.
Right-wing protesters have been standing guard outside the Constitutional Tribunal to prevent the Tusk government from installing the new judge, but the surge of police dispersed these efforts.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk arrives for the EU summit in Brussels, Thursday, June 18, 2026. (Omar Havana/AP Photo, File)
POLISH LEFT PUSHING ABORTION LIBERALIZATION THROUGH PARLIAMENT DESPITE LOOMING PRESIDENTIAL VETO
Beata Szydlo, a PiS-aligned member of the European Parliament, posted a video of the situation to social media on Friday night — calling it a “violation of all democratic principles.”

“Shocking scenes in Poland. Police, dispatched by the Tusk government, have forced their way into the independent Constitutional Tribunal. Security personnel guarding the building and the Tribunal’s documents have been removed,” she wrote on social media. “The Vice-President of the Tribunal is being denied entry to the premises.”

articles.headline: AI law firm Crosby bids on disintegrating, famed firm Weil Gotshal
keyFacts: AI-first law firm Crosby offered to buy assets and hire lawyers from the declining firm Weil, Gotshal and Manges, TechCrunch confirmed.
Weil Gotshal confirmed it is preparing to vote on dissolution following leadership departures and a failed merger.
The financial terms of Crosby's bid were not disclosed and there is no guarantee the offer will succeed.
body: Like a real-life episode of “Suits,” the demise of famed white-shoe Wall Street law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges has been the talk of the legal industry this week. And now Silicon Valley has entered the picture.

Two-year-old AI-first law firm Crosby has put in a bid to buy some of the assets of Weil Gotshal, including its trademark, its brand, and some unspecified internal data, TechCrunch has confirmed. Separately, it is also working to hire some of the firm’s 1,200 lawyers. The Information was first to report this offer.

The once-prestigious Weil Gotshal confirmed to the New York Times this week that it was preparing to vote on dissolution in the coming days. The wind-down is happening after the firm’s presumed leadership heir apparent turned down the role, a number of its top-producing lawyers left, and a hoped-for merger with its rival, Willkie Farr & Gallagher, was shelved, the Times reported.

Meanwhile, Crosby’s founders believe they are the future of law firms. Rather than selling their internally developed AI tech to existing firms like Harvey or Legora, Crosby is an actual law firm. It uses its AI to provide legal services at, the startup promises, a speed never before possible.

The startup has raised about $85 million, including a $60 million Series B round in March led by Lux and Index, with participation from its seed-lead Sequoia, Elad Gil, 01 Advisors, and Bain Capital Ventures. Crosby came out of stealth mode in 2025 armed with $5.8 million in seed money.

While no one has pointed to the rise of legal AI as a contributing factor to Weil Gotshal’s downfall, AI may be key to the legal industry’s future. Terms of the bid weren’t disclosed and there’s no guarantee that Crosby will prevail. But if it does, Weil Gotshal’s legacy could somehow rise from the ashes, transformed by an AI-first firm.

articles.headline: Leclerc fastest in Mexico City Grand Prix first practice
keyFacts: Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc recorded the fastest time in the first practice session at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli finished second and is poised to clinch his first world title by finishing ninth.
The FIA stated that American driver Colton Herta has now accumulated enough miles to secure the required Formula 1 superlicence.
body: - Published
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc led Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli in first practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, where the Italian is poised to clinch his first world title.
Leclerc was 0.659 seconds quicker than Antonelli, for whom a ninth-place finish will secure the championship regardless of any other results.

Only a victory by his team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can theoretically stop Antonelli becoming champion on Sunday. Even then, Antonelli only needs ninth place if Russell wins and 10th if Hamilton does.
Third quickest in the session was Mercedes reserve Frederik Vesti, driving Russell's car, ahead of Hamilton.
Mercedes were one of 10 teams to choose this session to do one of their mandatory rookie sessions. Only Ferrari had both race drivers in their cars.
Mexico City is chosen by many teams to run their mandatory rookie sessions because the first session is traditionally unrepresentative as a result of the dirty track surface.
Japanese Ayumu Iwasa, in for Max Verstappen at Red Bull, was fifth fastest, ahead of Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso.
McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Haas driver Oliver Bearman and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10.

Briton Freddie Slater's first outing at a grand prix weekend for Audi did not go to plan. Reliability problems limited his running to 14 laps - about half a standard mileage. But he did manage to get out for the final 20 minutes or so and set the 19th fastest time.
He was just behind another Briton, Luke Browning having his latest run in the Williams.
American Colton Herta, who Cadillac are considering promoting to F1 next year in place of Valtteri Bottas, was 22nd.
Governing body the FIA says Herta, a nine-time winner in Indycar, has now done enough miles to score the 40 points he needs to secure the superlicence required to race in F1.

articles.headline: Outcry prompts ‘Call of Duty’ to cut Seoul tragedy footage
keyFacts: Activision acknowledged an outcry in South Korea after including real-life footage from the 2022 Seoul crowd crush in its new game.
Victims' family organizations demanded the footage be removed, stating the developer lacked empathy and reproduced scenes of people receiving CPR.
Activision apologized and said it will completely remove the footage through a game update scheduled for Nov. 12.
body: American video game publisher Activision said Friday that it was removing controversial footage from its newly released “Call of Duty” game after an outcry in South Korea over the inclusion of real-life footage from a deadly 2022 Halloween crowd crush in Seoul.

Last week’s global release of “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” came days before the Oct. 29 anniversary of the disaster in the South Korean capital’s nightlife district of Itaewon, where a crowd of tens of thousands of partygoers surged beyond control in a narrow alley, causing nearly 160 deaths.

The game, which takes place amid a fictional North Korean invasion of the South, features about 10 seconds of heavily edited footage of the tragedy to illustrate what the aftermath of a Pyongyang attack might look like, though it does not refer to the Itaewon crowd crush directly.

Groups representing families of the crowd crush victims had demanded that the footage be removed, saying it was appalling that the game had directly reproduced actual scenes of people performing CPR “while victims lay on the cold streets amid chaos and desperation.”

“If the game developer has even the slightest sense of respect and empathy for the victims of the Itaewon disaster, it should promptly take corrective action,” the Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association and Itaewon Disaster Citizens’ Countermeasures Committee said in a joint statement Friday.
The California-based game publisher, Activision, apologized in a statement and said the footage would be completely removed through a game update scheduled for release Nov. 12.

“This game is a fictional work created to provide a realistic and immersive experience,” the company said, according to the South Korean public broadcaster MBC. “In using actual news footage in the game, we never intended to evoke any tragic incident, including the Itaewon disaster, or to trivialize the suffering associated with such tragedies.”

The controversy came as grieving families are still waiting for answers about authorities’ failure to prevent the disaster four years ago. Nearly two dozen officials have been charged in the investigation, which is still underway, while three former police officers have been jailed.
On Thursday, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung vowed that his government would “uncover the truth.”
“On that day, when what should have been a joyful autumn night turned into the scene of a horrific tragedy, the state was nowhere to be found,” he said in a statement on X.
Lee Jin Woo, whose younger sister was 28 when she died in the crowd crush, told NBC News that he had played the new “Call of Duty” game and didn’t notice the Itaewon footage at first.
“But after hearing about it and thinking it over, I began to realize the footage looked very similar,” said Lee, who works at a South Korean gaming company.
“The more I thought about it, the more I felt betrayed as a gamer,” he said. “After all, it was a game company and a game series that I had liked.”

The game’s premise, in which South Korean conscripts are thrust into defending their country alongside American soldiers after a North Korean invasion, has been controversial since before it was available to play.

Though the “Call of Duty” invasion is fictional, it draws on North Korea’s real-life capture of Seoul in 1950 during the Korean War. The conflict ended in 1953 with an armistice instead of a peace treaty, and the two Koreas remain technically at war.

Tensions between the North and South have escalated in recent weeks, with the two countries embroiled in a standoff along their heavily militarized border. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has rebuffed diplomatic outreach from Washington and Seoul as he continues to advance his nuclear and ballistic missile programs.

“Ultimately, whether we’re talking about an actual war or the Itaewon disaster, both involve the suffering of real people,” Lee Mi Hyun, a director at the Itaewon Disaster Citizens’ Countermeasures Committee, told NBC News in an interview.
“They’re turning that suffering into entertainment,” she said. “It’s an approach that seems to show absolutely no empathy for the people who experienced that suffering.”
Some South Korean lawmakers say the game should be taken as a warning.
“We need to pay attention to the question it raises,” Han Dong-hoon, an opposition legislator, said last week in a Facebook post. “If that day were to come again, would we be ‘prepared’?”

The game has also been defended by members of Lee’s governing Democratic Party such as Kim Han Kyu, who said there was “nothing wrong with playing a game set against the backdrop of North Korea’s nuclear weapons.”
“We are still technically under an armistice, aren’t we?” he said Thursday in a Facebook post. “Wouldn’t it be even stranger if no games depicted a war against North Korea?”

Others have used the game to criticize Lee’s conciliatory approach to North Korea, with opposition lawmaker Ahn Cheol Soo suggesting last week that the South Korean president try playing the game to correct his “naïve judgment” about the North Korean threat.

With its “Call of Duty” franchise struggling to sustain interest in recent years, the Microsoft-owned Activision used “Modern Warfare 4” to deliver what fans loved about its previous games: a hyperrealistic military shooter.

“I don’t think we were happy with every aspect of last year’s game, and we heard the feedback loud and clear,” Activision Chief Marketing Officer Tyler Bahl told “The Game Business Show” earlier this month.

“With ‘Modern Warfare 4,’ we’ve tried to adjust based on that feedback. It’s getting back to a grounded military shooter. Making it cinematic, making it authentic and bringing that edge back that ‘Call of Duty’ is known for,” he said.

That approach appears to have worked. As of Friday, “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” was the top-selling game in both South Korea and the United States on Steam, an online PC game distribution platform.
In its review, gaming website IGN said it was a “much-needed reminder of what ‘Call of Duty’ can be at its best, even if it can’t fully recapture the heights of its glory days.”

articles.headline: Ilhan Omar’s allies break ranks as ex-Dem insider says sham marriage allegations are ‘almost certainly true’
keyFacts: Former Democratic lawmaker Joe Radinovich claimed that allegations Representative Ilhan Omar married her brother are almost certainly true.
Federal investigators are examining Omar's finances and immigration history, having recently searched her Washington home, though no charges have been filed.
Omar has denied wrongdoing, and her campaign called Radinovich's statements false, biased, and without evidence.
body: A prominent Minnesota Democrat is breaking ranks with his party over Rep. Ilhan Omar — declaring allegations that she married her brother are “almost certainly true” and warning that questions about her finances aren’t going away, either.

Joe Randinovich, a former Minnesota state representative and well-connected Democratic operative, delivered the assessment in a series of posts on X Thursday, challenging the congresswoman’s longstanding denials and the party’s efforts to dismiss the allegations as a right-wing conspiracy.

“Democrats should understand that the allegation is almost certainly true — whatever conclusions they draw from that point could vary — and her denials calling it a right-wing, Islamophobic or racist conspiracy are almost certainly not,” Radinovich wrote.

The comments come as federal investigators continue to look into Omar’s immigration history and finances, with the Minnesota Democrat suggesting his party should stop reflexively defending the embattled congresswoman.

“And then I’d very, very careful about how I qualified on allegations around her finances — where her defense looks similar and where no meaningful questions have been answered publicly, and where any objective look at the evidence doesn’t look…great,” he added.
Radinovich’s comments quickly sparked confrontation with Briana Rose Lee, a Minneapolis Democratic activist who previously worked in Omar’s campaign operation.
“Joe. You aren’t stupid. You know this is a baseless and manufactured witch hunt. I’m actually surprised to see this from you,” Lee wrote. “It’s a new low.”
However, Randinovich didn’t back down.

“You’re right. I’m not stupid,” he responded, acknowledging that he has little confidence in President Trump’s Justice Department, and questioning the timing of the federal raid on Omar’s Washington DC residence.
Here’s the latest on the ongoing immigration investigation of Rep. Ilhan Omar
“Though it’s pretty notable that a DC judge signed off on it,” he added, before declaring that he’s “pretty confident this specific allegation is true.”
In a separate post, Radinovich doubled down on his stance, arguing that anyone who believes Omar’s denials must be ignoring a growing body of evidence.
“Vibes is what it would take to believe her at this point,” he wrote. “There’s plenty of evidence and sourcing available if you don’t dismiss it out of hand.”
The public break is particularly notable, due to Radinovich’s ties to the Minnesota Democratic establishment.

Radinovich served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2013 to 2015, managed Democrat Rick Nolan’s 2016 congressional campaign and ran Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey’s successful 2017 campaign. He later served as Frey’s chief of staff.
Ilhan Omar's relative timeline
Significant dates into Rep. Ilhan Omar’s past relationships, which point to a potential sham marriage with her brother.

1995— After four years in a refugee camp in Kenya because of the Somalian civil war, Omar and her family emigrate to the US.

2002 — Omar marries Ahmed Hirsi (right) in an Islamic ceremony. They applied for a marriage license, but, she said, “we never finalized the application and thus were never legally married.” They have two children.
2009 — Omar marries Ahmed Nur Said Elmi. Evidence points to Elmi being her brother, and that she married him so he could legally live in the US after the family wanted him out of the UK.
2012 — Omar still lived with Hirsi during this time, witnesses told the Post, and they had a third child this year. Elmi also reportedly leaves Minnesota this year.
2016 — The FBI and Department of Homeland Security investigate claims Omar married her brother, as she runs for Minnesota’s legislature.
2017 — Omar’s divorce from Elmi is finalized.
2018 — Omar officially marries Hirsi. She runs for Congress for the first time and wins.
2019 — Omar leaves Hirsi for Tim Mynett (left), a political consultant who is paid by her campaign. They marry the next year.

He also played a role in two unsuccessful Democratic primary challenges against Omar, working with Don Samuels in 2022 and 2024.

Omar, who represents Minnesota’s heavily Democratic 5th Congressional District, has repeatedly denied allegations that she married her brother, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, in 2009 as part of an alleged immigration fraud scheme.
Homeland Security Investigation agents raided Omar’s Washington D.C. home on Oct. 12, seizing her passport, phone and computer.

Federal investigators are examining whether Omar or her late father, Nur Mohamed, fraudulently provided information on citizenship paperwork decades ago. The investigation could potentially have consequences for her citizenship status.

During former President Barack Obama’s administration, feds opened an investigation into the alleged marriage scheme in 2016. The probe was open until 2021, but was closed by the Biden administration.
No criminal charges have been filed against Omar over the allegations, and her office continues to dismiss the claims as “politically motivated smears.”
Omar’s campaign responded to Radinovich’s claims to Fox News Digital on Friday.

“Joe is a deeply troubled individual whose demons have sadly manifested as an irrational obsession with Congresswoman Omar after managing two losing campaigns against her,” the campaign said to the outlet.
“His claims are false, biased, and without any evidence. While he was once seen as a rising star within the party, Joe is now widely recognized as a shill for Republican and Corporate money.”

articles.headline: Treasury flags $8B in suspicious foreign-directed transfers through US money services firms
keyFacts: Treasury's FinCEN identified over $8 billion in suspicious foreign-directed wire transfers sent through U.S. money services businesses.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration stopped nearly $190 million in fraudulent funds and returned over $100 million to victims.
The Treasury Department issued guidelines urging banks to scrutinize nonprofits' donors and funding streams to prevent potential money laundering.
body: The Trump administration uncovered what it says is more than $8 billion in potentially fraudulent cross-border wire payments that were made under foreign agents’ direction, issuing new guidelines for nonprofits who take foreign money, executing multiple FBI search warrants and building out a large-scale indictment.

The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) within the Treasury Department said it identified suspicious wire payments from 2021 to 2025 that were sent through U.S.-based money services businesses at the direction of foreign agents.

"When greed meets negligence, the American people suffer," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Under President Trump and Vice President Vance’s leadership, Treasury stopped nearly $190 million in funds tied to overseas fraud and returned more than $100 million to U.S. victims. We are working with the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud to help prevent this kind of abuse from happening again, in Minnesota or anywhere else."
WHITE HOUSE LAUNCHES INTERACTIVE MAP TRACKING BILLIONS IN SUSPECTED FRAUD

At a Friday press conference, Bessent said: "In the weeks following my visit, Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, known as FinCEN, issued a geographic targeting order to trace criminal networks.
That diverts funds overseas and ensures that taxpayer dollars go to the American people, not terror groups like Al Shabaab."

He added that the Treasury Department has investigations in the U.S. and abroad into "Al-Shabaab, its networks and its enablers. Since the start of the Trump administration, FinCen data have also supported the law enforcement effort that led to the arrest and charging of 115 fraudsters, as well as 75 convictions and nearly 3,000 subpoenas across Minnesota."

Bessent said that on Thursday, "IRS-CI assisted with investigative activity at several sites suspected of fraud. I want to give a shout-out to our great officers at IRS-CI. They don't get much press, but they are quietly one of the most affected groups in the United States government for fighting fraud."

Bessent, FBI Director Kash Patel , Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz and Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson held a news conference in Minnesota to detail the substantial fraud uncovered and FBI Minnesota's actions.

"This FBI follows the money," Patel said at the Friday press conference. "This FBI will put in prison anyone who commits fraud anywhere in the world against any American citizen. Thanks to President Trump, we finally have a commander-in-chief who prioritized the initiative to go after the fraudsters with the full force of government."

The Treasury Department issued a notice urging banks to scrutinize nonprofits’ donors, funding streams and ties to other groups and governments. FinCEN says the arrangements could obscure the ultimate recipients and potentially be exploited for money laundering or terrorist financing .
WATCHDOG UNLEASHES DATABASE TO EXPOSE 'LOOPHOLES' AS $5B IN FOREIGN CASH FLOODS US NONPROFITS

The notice noted that bad actors commit fraud in three forms of abuse: sham charities allegedly diverting funds to illicit activity, charity-related fraud that enriches the people running the scheme, and embezzlement by insiders at legitimate organizations.

Salim Said, a co-conspirator in the Feeding Our Future case , was sentenced to 30 years in prison this week after being convicted on 21 counts tied to a scheme that defrauded a federal child nutrition program of $49 million.

At the end of last year, reports and social media coverage by Shirley exposed a network of daycare centers, like the "Quality Learing (sic) Center," that were allegedly fraudulent and operated mostly by Somali immigrants.
MINNESOTA MAN CAPTURED IN SOMALIA AFTER ALLEGEDLY HELPING ORCHESTRATE $250M CHILD NUTRITION FRAUD SCHEME

The reports sparked swift action from the administration, and former Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem deployed DHS and ICE agents to the streets of Minneapolis to catch and deport Somali immigrants in the country illegally. The deployment sparked a clash between local residents and federal agents that exploded into violent riots across the Twin Cities.

The Treasury secretary has previously taken aim at fraud and bad actors funding nonprofit organizations in the U.S. In April, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) tightened tax-exempt reporting requirements in an effort to uncover nonprofit funding being used for "extremist activity" and "hiding fraud."

"Tax-exempt status is not immunity from scrutiny," Treasury Assistant Secretary and acting IRS chief counsel Ken Kies wrote in a statement. "If an organization receives public funds or tax-deductible donations, it should be prepared to show who controls the money and where it goes."
CRUZ PUSHES BILL TO HOLD TAX-EXEMPT SPONSORS ACCOUNTABLE AS DOJ PROBES SINGHAM NETWORK

Bessent has also been involved with the Department of Justice’s grand jury probe into the nonprofit network of Neville Roy Singham . Sources at Treasury told Fox News Digital that Bessent met with Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon and discussed Singham’s previously held accounts at the bank, which Singham used to distribute funds to a number of nonprofits.
HOUSE PANEL WARNS SINGHAM-LINKED NONPROFITS: COMPLY WITH SUBPOENAS OR FACE CONGRESS

Singham, a 72-year-old American who sold his tech company for $785 million in 2017 and now lives in Shanghai, has funneled $278 million into the broad network of nonprofits since 2017, according to a Fox News Digital investigation. These groups regularly organize and participate in anti-ICE, anti-Israel and pro-Iran demonstrations .
Singham has not been charged, and the investigation at the Southern District of New York remains ongoing.

articles.headline: Android 17 adoption hits a staggering 1% – why you really should update now
keyFacts: Android 17 adoption has reached only 1% of active devices since its June 2026 release, according to data from heise.de and Android Studio.
Data shows that approximately 40% of Android users have not yet upgraded to Android 14 or later versions.
Upgrading to Android 17 provides improved features and better security for eligible devices.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways:
- Less than 1% of active devices run Android 17, according to recent data.
- Roughly 40% of Android users have yet to upgrade to Android 14.
- Upgrading to the latest OS brings more features and better security.

Android 17 adoption hasn’t been speedy. According to the most recent data from heise.de via Android Studio, as reported by Android Authority, Android 17 has reached just 1% of active devices since its release in June 2026.

While Android 16 is finally the most used Google OS for Android devices, at 25.4% of active Android devices, these distribution figures indicate that getting users to upgrade to even newer software is an uphill battle.

It’s true that Android 17 has had less time to reach devices than Android 16 did when the previous distribution snapshot was published, but the minuscule adoption rate underscores how slowly the latest release is infiltrating the Android ecosystem.
More from ZDNET

Plus, the data show that more Android users than not are running versions that are many years old. I’m all for not fixing what’s not broken, but when Android 14 is the second most widely used version (15.% of devices are still running it), while Android 15 trails not far behind at 14.7%, there’s a pretty large chunk of individuals who may be putting themselves (and their data) at risk.

And it doesn’t end there. Android 13 and Android 11 are still on the table for 11.8% and 10.1% of users, with almost another 10% still using Android 12. That’s about another 30% of users still running Android 13 or older.
Though the numbers indicate that almost 60% of active Android devices are running Android 14 or newer, about 40% of users haven’t even upgraded to Android 14 or later.

While the numbers are staggering, they’re not surprising. Android updates typically lag behind iOS updates. While the iPhone and its software are both designed, controlled, and distributed by Apple, Android updates must roll out from a single starting point to a wider array of mobile devices and systems to reach users. While Google is responsible for the core of the Android system, those updates must then be curated, reviewed, and pushed to every device that uses Android. This includes phones from Google, Samsung, Nothing, and more, which usually requires adaptations from each manufacturer. Apple’s updates are often adopted faster because there’s no middle entity between iOS and the user, while Android’s process is rather fragmented.
Why should you consider upgrading to Android 17

It’s always good practice to keep your device updated to the latest available software that your system allows. There are a few great reasons why those eligible for Android 17 should upgrade, including improved features — like the ability to “bubble” apps and stop network snoops and SMS blasters.

Plus, it’s the most proactive thing you can do for your device. Software updates usually include improvements to your phone’s operation, speed, security, and more, and it’s an easy (and free) way to keep your phone healthy.

articles.headline: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
keyFacts: Researchers led by NASA scientist Yang Liu showed that the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 formed at least 4.1 billion years ago.
Teghaza 001 is only the third genuinely ancient Martian meteorite known to science, alongside Allan Hills 84001 and Black Beauty.
Scientists stated that large impacts act as a filter, meaning weak Martian rocks cannot survive the journey to Earth.
body: Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger. Until now, only two genuinely ancient Martian meteorites were known: Allan Hills 84001, found in Antarctica, and a jumbled rock from northwest Africa nicknamed Black Beauty. Now we have a third one.

A team led by Yang Liu, a planetary scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, has shown that a Martian meteorite called Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. “It’s very old and similar to some of the oldest rocks on Earth,” Liu says.
A filtered collection

“We don’t fully understand why old Martian rocks are so rare on Earth,” Liu said. Part of the answer may lie in how a piece of Mars gets here. It takes a large impact to launch a rock off the planet, and not every rock can survive that. “If the impact hits into loose powder, it may not get cemented to become a rock and fly off Mars’ gravity,” Liu said. “So the natural impact already acts as a filter. Weak rocks do not make it off Mars.”
That left scientists with a biased collection.

“Even to date, none of our collected Martian meteorites are similar to what we found on the surface,” Liu said. The partial exception is Black Beauty, which has a bulk chemistry that matches orbital measurements. But Black Beauty is a mix of soil and many small rock fragments. Teghaza 001 is a single, intact igneous rock.

articles.headline: JD Vance Admits He’s ‘Jealous’ Over Trump’s Fixation On MAGA Senator’s Ass
keyFacts: Vice President JD Vance stated at a town hall that he was jealous of Donald Trump's repeated praise for Senator Jon Husted's body.
Trump claimed his public compliments about Husted's physique helped the Republican senator gain twelve points in the polls against Sherrod Brown.
Vance held the town hall appearance to energize Republican voters ahead of the midterm elections next week.
body: President Donald Trump’s fixation on male Republican lawmakers’ bodies and especially their buttocks isn’t sitting too well with Vice President JD Vance.

Vance appeared Thursday at a Fox News town hall in Fort Worth, Texas, with the intent of energizing GOP voters ahead of the midterms next week. When host Jesse Watters asked about the president’s repeated comments on Sen. Jon Husted’s (R-Ohio) backside, the vice president acknowledged he was envious.
“First of all, I’m jealous. The president’s never said that about me,” he quipped. “I’ve got to get back in the gym maybe and draw that particular piece of praise.”

After describing Trump’s eyebrow-raising remark as one of his “favorites,” the vice president noted, “The president, as you know, is at heart a comedian, and he loves to get up there and shake things up a little bit. I just think it’s a good example of a politician who doesn’t take himself so seriously.”
Vance’s response to Trump’s Husted remarks can be found at about 5:18 in the video below.
Trump first gushed over Husted’s physique at an Oct. 20 rally in North Carolina, quickly zooming in on the senator’s derrière.

“His ass, shit, it’s like, it’s like a pile of muscle,” he said. “Then I looked at his legs, and I said, ‘Man, his feet are big.’ Then I looked at his shoulders, and I tapped him on the shoulder, and it actually hurt my hand. He’s like a piece of steel. I said, ‘This guy’s a monster.’”

While Trump prefaced those remarks by claiming he’d “never studied the body of a man before,” CNN’s Anderson Cooper proved him wrong a day later with a cheeky compilation of clips showing the president publicly complimenting men like Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.) and Larry Nordone, who is married to Sen. Darline Graham (R-S.C.), on their looks.

Seemingly pleased with the media discourse, Trump reiterated his enthusiasm for Husted’s “great” and “very powerful ass” on TikTok this week, claiming his comments had prompted the senator to jump “12 points in the ratings.”
In reality, many polls show Husted with a slight edge over his Democratic opponent, former Sen. Sherrod Brown ― though it’s unclear whether Trump’s commentary has had an impact on that tight race.

In his chat with Watters on Thursday, Vance acknowledged that Husted has a “very nice body,” before emphasizing that he will “make a much better senator for the people of the United States of America than the lunatic he’s running against,” referring to Brown.

For many, however, the joke appears to be wearing thin. Elsewhere during the town hall, Vance initially responded to a young voter’s question about housing affordability for families with yet another crack about Husted’s butt.

The clip quickly went viral, with former White House deputy press secretary Sarah Matthews noting on X: “I genuinely cannot believe this is a real exchange between a voter and the Vice President of the United States.”

articles.headline: A working-class Alaskan Native takes on a ‘multimillionaire’ Republican for seat in Congress
keyFacts: Independent commercial fisher Bill Hill is challenging Republican Congressman Nick Begich for Alaska's sole seat in the House.
Hill emphasizes rising living costs and union support, while national Democrats back his campaign.
Recent polls show Hill trailing Begich by single digits ahead of the November 3 election.
body: As Republicans fight to maintain their narrow majority in Congress, they face a unique challenge in Alaska – not from a Democrat, but from an independent commercial fisher and first-time candidate running to flip the state’s lone House seat.

Bill Hill, who is an Alaska Native and has worked in education and construction, has positioned himself as a working-class candidate who will fight to make life more affordable for people like himself and his family.

Like voters across the country, Alaskans are deeply worried about affordability and the rising cost of basic necessities. Hill counts himself among the voters who have felt squeezed by high fuel prices driven up by Donald Trump’s war on Iran.

“When the spring fuel barge showed up in my home town of Naknek this spring, I went from paying $118 to fill my truck up to over $200,” Hill said. “Our gas went from $6.70 a gallon to almost $9 a gallon.”

Hill’s campaign to unseat the Republican congressman Nick Begich has gained momentum in the final weeks before the 3 November election, as national Democrats line up behind him and ad spending ramps up. The non-partisan Cook Political Report recently shifted the race from “likely Republican” to “leans Republican”, with the district favoring Republicans by six percentage points.

Recent polls showed Hill trailing Begich by single digits, but Hill’s support grows when voters learn more about his background, as he works to boost his name recognition. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee added the race to its coveted “red to blue” program in September.

Hill has not specified whether he would caucus with Democrats if elected. This cycle, he is among several independents challenging Republicans in red states, including Senate candidates Dan Osborn in Nebraska and Todd Achilles in Idaho.

In Alaska, Begich may benefit from being the only Republican in the four-way general election contest run under the state’s ranked-choice system. Polls suggest support for Democrat Eric Hafner, who is serving time in a federal prison in New York and has no apparent links to the state, could complicate Hill’s path.
Hill has staked his campaign on his ability to personally relate to the economic pain and frustrations of his fellow Alaskans.

“I have spent a life being in the ditches, in the school hallways, on the back decks of fishing boats with hard-working people, running a small business like so many Alaskans do, and I know what the struggles and challenges that we face are,” Hill said. “I also know what our hopes and dreams are.”

He noted the cost of heating fuel nearly doubled, from $4.50 a gallon to $8.30, while price increases in some of Alaska’s more remote villages have soared even higher. In places such as Ambler and Shungnak, Indigenous villages that sit along the Kobuk River near the Arctic circle, the price of a gallon of gas has surpassed $25.
“This is crushing Alaskans,” Hill said. “We are feeling the crunch every single day.”

More than one in three Alaskan households aren’t earning enough income to cover housing, food, childcare and other essential expenses, according to a report by the United Way of Anchorage and Alaska 211 published earlier this month.

In 2024, Begich, the conservative son of a prominent Democratic family in Alaska, narrowly ousted the incumbent Democrat, Mary Peltola, who is currently running for US Senate. Though Trump won the state by a resounding 13%, Begich prevailed by just 2.4%.
Like Peltola, Hill is a supporter of gun rights, in line with Alaska’s strong hunting tradition, and is a supporter of both the oil industry and the renewable energy industry.

Hill cited the impacts on Alaskans of cuts to the Snap nutrition-assistance program and Medicaid, the expiration of Affordable Care Act tax credits, Trump’s tariffs, federal job losses in Alaska, and the cancellation of several Alaskan renewable energy projects by the Trump administration as contributing factors to added costs facing Alaskans, with many of the cuts enacted by the president’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act set to go into effect in 2027.
“It is getting very, very difficult for working people in Alaska to get by,” Hill said, charging that his opponent was a “multimillionaire working for billionaires”.

With his reported assets valued at $119,000, Hill has sought to highlight the vast wealth gap between himself and his opponent, who is worth at least $7.4m. “He’s somebody who doesn’t represent the everyday Alaskan in his work,” Hill added.
Begich’s office did not respond to multiple requests for comment, but previously denied his wealth affects his voting record.

“Congressman Begich’s personal finances have no impact on his legislative decisionmaking process,” Silver Prout, a spokesperson for Begich’s congressional office, told the Anchorage Press in an email.
Begich praised the passage of Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act, calling it a “transformative victory”, and has continued supporting Trump’s war in Iran.

Hill, a Dena’ina Athabascan Native Alaskan, has worked as a commercial fisher since he was eight years old and continues to do so. He has also worked union construction jobs with Laborers’ Local 341, and worked for 25 years in education as a union member teacher, principal and school district superintendent.
Alaska has one of the highest union density rates in the US. As of 2025, 18.1% of all workers in the state were union members, the third highest rate in the US, behind Hawaii and New York.

More than 20 labor organizations, including the Alaska AFL-CIO, have endorsed Hill’s campaign. Begich, meanwhile, has signed on to the National Right to Work Act and has a 0% lifetime voting score by the AFL-CIO, the largest federation of labor unions in the US.

“Unions need more support in Congress, and we see attacks on trying to tear down their power in this nation,” Hill said. “At the end of the day, unions built the middle class of this country, and they’re the ones who can do it again.”

articles.headline: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost concerns
keyFacts: US stocks dropped sharply on Friday as investors grew increasingly concerned about the high costs of artificial intelligence investments.
Intel shares fell up to 30 percent after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market and increased AI spending.
Intel finance chief David Zinsner stated that the firm does not expect positive cash flow this year and forecast lower-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue.
body: - Published
US stocks have continued to slide as concerns continue to intensify over the increasing costs of the artificial intelligence (AI) build out.

Shares in Intel continued their overnight slide into early trading on Friday, falling as much as 30% after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market even as it plans to increase spending on AI.
Amazon shares fell as far as 6% before recovering after its reported earnings on Thursday evening fell short of investors' expectations.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange opened on Friday at its lowest level in more than two months, down 2.5%, as other tech stocks including Reddit and Roblox continued to fall.
The losses follow the value of Google owner Alphabet plunging by more than $500bn on Thursday after it revealed its own AI summaries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.
Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading, down 1% after Thursday's massive slide.
The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere, with Intel on track to lose more than $130bn in value after its earnings update rattled investors.
On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect positive cash flow this year, and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.
"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.
In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.

articles.headline: Forget tainted candy: The scariest thing on Halloween is parked in your driveway
keyFacts: Pedestrians under 18 are three times more likely to be struck and killed by cars on Halloween than any other day.
Experts attribute the danger to increased child and driver traffic at dusk, impaired partygoers, and larger vehicles.
Cities such as New York, St. Petersburg, and Seattle are implementing car-free zones to create safer environments for trick-or-treaters.
body: Arial Meehan, 9, center, dressed as a crazy cat lady, smiles as she walks down the street with other trick-or-treaters on Halloween 2018. | Natalie Kolb/MediaNews Group/Reading Eagle via Getty Images

As is the custom, millions of children in the United States will be out in the streets this Halloween to trick-or-treat , decked out in costumes. Also as is custom, adults will fret about the mostly mythical dangers children may face. Once upon a time it was razor blades in apples; this year, it’s rainbow fentanyl in candy. But while fears of children receiving narcotic-spiked treats are unfounded , there is a very real danger that America’s children face on this most hallowed of evenings: cars .

That’s because pedestrians under the age of 18 are three times more likely to be struck and killed by a car on Halloween than any other day of the year. A 2026 analysis of federal crash records found that 45 children were killed while walking on Halloween between 2010 and 2024, more than any other day. That risk grows to 10 times more likely for children aged 4 to 8 years old, according to a study from 2019 in JAMA Pediatrics .

“You’re going to have increased numbers of children, including younger children who are out on the streets,” said Lois Lee , a professor of pediatrics and emergency medicine at Harvard Medical School. “At the same time, you have adults who are driving, and especially this year on a Monday, people will be driving home from work. If children are in costume, they may be wearing darker clothing … which makes them harder to detect.”

The JAMA Pediatrics study from 2019 corroborates this, noting that Halloween “may heighten pedestrian traffic risk, because celebrations occur at dusk, masks restrict peripheral vision, costumes limit visibility, street-crossing safety is neglected, and some partygoers are impaired by alcohol.” It’s the kind of lethal combination that can turn a fun occasion into a deadly nightmare. Adult victims included, the risk of death to all pedestrians was 43 percent higher on Halloween compared to a regular evening.

But what happens on Halloween isn’t an isolated incident. After gun injuries , motor vehicle injuries are the second leading cause of death among children in the US overall. And with pedestrian fatalities (both adult and child) at a 40-year high in the US, it’s worth asking why children roaming the streets is so inherently deadly, and what can be done about it.

“Sometimes when you talk about this issue, you get pushback from people and people say, ‘Well, of course, you have more children on the streets, of course, more children are going to die,’” Doug Gordon , a writer and podcast host who advocates for safer streets and cities, told me. “But that accepts a baseline level of danger that I think we as a society have in fact accepted on the other 364 days of the year.”

There are broader reasons for why streets have gotten even more dangerous for pedestrians recently. One is that drivers are distracted — not just by their phones, but increasingly by the infotainment systems that come as a part of newer cars. A more pressing issue is the increasing size of cars in the US; SUVs make up half of all car sales in the US, and are much more likely to kill pedestrians in crashes than smaller vehicles. “Mass times [acceleration] is force,” Gordon summed up. “When you increase the mass of something, you’re going to increase the force at which it interacts with a small vulnerable child.”

But the biggest reason may be that American streets and cities are designed for cars , and not people. As Charles Marohn — founder and president of Strong Towns and an expert on urban planning and civil engineering — has argued, engineers who design streets prioritize getting cars as quickly from point A to point B over everything else. One recent example : A traffic safety committee in Utah could not find any way to make the five-lane road crossing to a school safer for students aside from just removing the crosswalk altogether.

But there is a lot that can be done to make streets safer, for future Halloweens and every other day of the year. In the short term, cities and towns can build on open streets programs implemented after the Covid-19 pandemic began, which involve closing certain streets to car traffic to allow for more public space. Notably, New York City announced a “Trick or Streets” plan that would see 100 car-free zones in effect from 4 to 8 pm on Halloween this year. And the Big Apple isn’t alone, as Henry Grabar reported for Slate : less dense and more car-dependent cities like St. Petersburg, Florida and Seattle will also either close off the city center for Halloween or actually allow residents to apply for permits that can close off their neighborhoods to car traffic .

In the long run, Gordon believes that places around the US should be able to pass what is known as the popsicle test , where a kid should be able to safely walk to a store, buy a popsicle, and return home before it melts. In essence, every city should be designed to be friendly and traversable to the most vulnerable in our communities. “If you start thinking along those lines, then I think you start thinking along the lines of what infrastructure is needed to make that possible, where I would feel comfortable letting my kid do that,” Gordon said. “Halloween is like a giant version of the popsicle test because it’s not just your kid, it’s every kid in the neighborhood.”

Designing safer streets for children goes beyond safety — it would make for a better Halloween. “Having sidewalks and good lighting is a good preventive measure, not just for injury prevention, but also just general health,” Lee told me, “because that encourages everybody in the neighborhood to walk, exercise, and get outside, which is better for everybody’s health as well.”
And if their safety isn’t enough motivation, designing dense, walkable cities could even lead to bigger candy hauls for kids.

“When you build a city that’s safer, so that kids can walk around by themselves and not be worried about getting hit by a car, or the parents being worried about them being hit by a car, it’s just better,” Gordon said. “It’s awesome. They’re independent. It’s fun. And on Halloween, they get a lot of candy.”
Correction, October 31, 4 pm ET: A previous version of this story had an inaccurate definition of the equation for force.
Update, October 30, 2026, 10 am ET: This story has been updated to include new federal crash data.
